title: Non-adjacent triples of cells in a triangular grid: proofs of three conjectured generating functions
summary: Let $\Tn$ be the triangular grid of side $n$, with its $n^2$ unit cells, and let two cells be side-adjacent if they share an edge and point-adjacent if they share a vertex. We count the orbits of $3$-element sets of pairwise non-adjacent cells under the rotation group $C_3$ and under the full symmetry group $D_3$ of $\Tn$. Three of the four resulting sequences are OEIS A397730, A397731 and A397732, for each of which the only formula on record is a generating function conjectured by Sean A.\ Irvine on 14 July 2026. We prove all three conjectures. The route is Burnside's lemma, together with exact lattice counts for each fixed-point term. The side-adjacency graph turns out to be bipartite, so its triangle count vanishes, and the triangles of the point-adjacency graph have a clean structural description, which gives that count too. Along the way we obtain the first explicit closed forms for the three sequences, each a quasi-polynomial of degree $6$ and period $3$, $6$, $3$ respectively. The same machinery settles the fourth member of the family, whose closed form has been recorded at A289230 without proof since 2017, and the labeled count A289224 that feeds it.

title: Equidistribution of mesh patterns of length 2 on involutions
summary: We classify all 1024 length-two mesh patterns on involutions into exactly 287 equidis- tribution classes, consisting of 262 trivial classes and 25 nontrivial classes. Since many bi- jections on arbitrary permutations do not preserve the involution condition, our proofs use several involution-preserving bijections, including conjugation and local adjacent-transposition operations, transposition of the RSK recording tableau, prefix-rank swap bijections and marked-occurrence bijections. In particular, we establish the equidistribution of INV-099, a nontrivial class closely related to the unrestricted Class 69, by adapting the marked- occurrence bijection of Zhang and Zhao through a symmetric closure of the marked set. We also obtain explicit distribution formulas and recurrences for several classes, including continued fractions obtained by specializing known labeled Motzkin-path formulas and rational expressions derived from paired skew decompositions of involutions.

title: Sages and Their Anonymous Slips
summary: Before the game, the sages agree on a finite set of symbols and on a rule for choosing one of them. They are then seated in an unknown order, either in a row or around a circle with a common clockwise direction. Each sage sees only the adjacent sage or sages and secretly writes one symbol. The slips are then mixed, so nobody learns who wrote which symbol; everyone learns only how many times each symbol occurred. The aim is that every sage should be able to independently reconstruct the entire seating. We ask for the smallest number of distinct symbols that makes this possible. We also consider a version in which the seats have fixed public labels, and each sage is told the label of their own seat. For large numbers of sages, the minimum number of symbols is proportional to the square of the number of sages, up to a constant factor. Several small cases can be settled exactly. Four sages in a row need exactly two symbols, and so do five sages on a circle. Six sages on a circle need exactly three symbols, both with and without labeled seats; we give a short explicit rule. Five sages in a row with labeled seats also need exactly three symbols. Without seat labels, two symbols are impossible, and four are sufficient; whether three symbols suffice remains open.

title: Characteristic Chow Polynomials of Layered-Permutation Intervals
summary: We study characteristic Chow polynomials of principal intervals in generalized subword order, equivalently of pattern-containment intervals below layered permutations. A terminal-chain recurrence and canonical rightmost embeddings yield a recursive rational generating function for every fixed number of layers, governed by a universal denominator. In the two-layer case we obtain an explicit kernel, prove canonical interlacing when one layer has size at most four, and prove eventual interlacing at every fixed width by a Laguerre limit. We also treat two families with unboundedly many layers. Singleton-prefix intervals have a closed Delannoy-Jacobi gamma polynomial and form real-rooted interlacing sequences. Singleton-sandwich intervals admit rational three-variable series and a marked-slot formula for all gamma coefficients. Their central-layer-two and central-layer-three slices are real-rooted, with interlacing under growth from two to three. For each fixed pair of singleton flanks, a Laguerre differential transform proves eventual interlacing as the central layer grows. These results exhibit composition intervals as a structured testing ground for positivity and root-location questions for Chow polynomials of posets.
comment: 32 pages. Supplementary verification code and scope reports included as ancillary files

title: The minimum number of wheel-saturating edges
summary: Let $G$ be an $H$-free graph and $e$ be a non-edge of $G$. We say $e$ is an $H$-saturating edge of $G$, if $G+e$ contains a copy of $H$. We denote by $f_H(n,m)$ the minimum number of $H$-saturating edges of an $n$-vertex $H$-free graph with exactly $m$ edges. In this paper, we show that $f_{W_{2k+1}}(n,ex(n,F_{2k+1})+1)= \begin{cases} \ell -k, &(k-2)\ell \ \text{is even}, 2(\ell-k)-1, &(k-2)\ell \ \text{is odd}, \end{cases}$ and $f_{W_{2k}}(n,ex(n,F_{2k})+1)=\left(\frac{2}{33}+o(1)\right)n^2.$ At the same time, we characterize the corresponding extremal graphs.

title: Nonintersecting Unit Diagonals in Odd Square Arrays
summary: Let $D(n)$ be the maximum number of unit-square diagonals in an $n\times n$ square array such that no two selected diagonals share an endpoint and no unit square contains both diagonals. We prove that, for every odd positive integer $n$, $D(n)=n(n+1)/2+\lfloor(n+1)/6\rfloor$. The matching lower bound was established by Boyland, Roth, Pintér, Laukó, Schoenfield, and Wasielewski. We obtain the upper bound by transforming any admissible selection $M$ in a $(2k-1)\times(2k-1)$ square array into an isometric path cover of the $k\times k$ vertex grid with at most $2k^2-|M|$ paths. An auxiliary matching decomposes the original vertices into alternating paths. On each such path, all segments between blocks are either of type $da$ or of type $bc$. Projecting these paths to the block grid gives coordinate-monotone sequences, which become geodesics when diagonal steps are expanded. The Fisher--Fitzpatrick theorem then yields the sharp upper bound. We also describe a Lean verification of the upper-bound reduction, with the grid-cover theorem supplied as an explicit hypothesis.
comment: Lean source code included as ancillary files

title: Second largest eigenvalue thresholds for the vertex-connectivity of regular graphs
summary: Let $λ_2(G)$ and $κ(G)$ denote the second largest adjacency eigenvalue and the vertex-connectivity of a graph $G$. For a non-complete $r$-regular graph $G$, Fiedler's inequality $λ_2(G)\ge r-κ(G)$ shows that $λ_2(G)<r-t$ forces $κ(G)\ge t+1$. The best such bound is known for $t=1$, by Zhang and Wang, and for $t=2$ with $r\ge4$, by Zhang. In this paper, for every $r\ge3$ and every integer $t$ with $2\le t\le r-1$, we give an upper bound on $λ_2(G)$ that forces an $r$-regular graph $G$ to satisfy $κ(G)\ge t+1$, and we determine exactly when this bound is best possible. For $\frac{r+2}{2}\le t\le r-1$, Fiedler's bound $r-t$ is already best possible. For $2\le t<\frac{r+2}{2}$, it is replaced by one of two explicit algebraic numbers, and the sign of an explicit polynomial $W(r,t)$, which never vanishes, decides which one applies. Each of the two numbers is attained exactly when $(r,t)$ satisfies an explicit arithmetic condition, and every extremal graph then consists of two cliques and an independent cut of size $t$. In this range our bound also improves a bound of Zhang that holds for every such $t$.

title: Explicit strong blocking sets and minimal codes from expander graphs using a new graph parameter
summary: A strong blocking set is a set of points in a finite projective space that intersects every hyperplane of the space in a spanning set of the hyperplane. These objects have been studied both in finite geometry and coding theory due to their equivalence with minimal codes. We give an explicit construction of strong blocking sets using expander graphs that improves the explicit construction of Alon et al. (Noga Alon, Anurag Bishnoi, Shagnik Das, Alessandro Neri, Strong blocking sets and minimal codes from expander graphs. Transactions of the American Mathematical Society ) by introducing a new geometrically motivated graph parameter that is better suited for this problem. Using this approach, we improve the constant $C$ in the explicit construction of a strong blocking set of size $C (q+1) k$ in the $(k - 1)$-dimensional projective space over $\mathbb{F}_q$ for every prime power $q \geq 7$.

title: Minimum orders of clique oddomorphism counterexamples
summary: An oddomorphism to $K_n$ is a proper colouring with $n$ colours in which every vertex is designated odd or even, every vertex has in each other colour class a number of neighbours of its own parity, and every colour class contains an odd number of odd vertices. We prove that an oddomorphism witness to $K_n$ on at most $n+6$ vertices contains a $K_n$ minor with every branch meeting the witness's specified odd set. The conclusion holds inside any graph containing the witness and therefore applies to weak oddomorphisms. The bound is sharp: for every $n\ge8$ the minimum order of a graph admitting a weak oddomorphism to $K_n$ but having no $K_n$ minor is exactly $n+7$. The extremal example is a fifteen-vertex graph with an oddomorphism to $K_8$, obtained from the doubled theta graph of Kriesell and Mohr by adding one vertex adjacent to the seven roots; we give a structural proof that it has no $K_8$ minor, including their counting argument for the rooted case. A separate technical companion records further results on related root-apex graphs, an attachment theorem and a bounded nine-colour statement, together with their computational provenance; none of it is used here. The results do not resolve the unrestricted clique-target problem.
comment: 64 pages, main article and technical companion combined; includes computational provenance and verifier source

title: A proof of Wang's planar D-coloring conjecture
summary: We prove Wang's planar D-coloring conjecture. A D-coloring of a graph is a proper edge coloring in which every subgraph isomorphic to $K_4$ minus an edge is rainbow. Wang conjectured that every planar graph of maximum degree $Δ$ has a D-coloring with 9 colors if $Δ=4$, 10 colors if $Δ=5$, and $2Δ-1$ colors if $Δ\ge 6$. Hu, Kong and Wang proved the cases $Δ\le 5$ and $Δ\ge 33$. We prove the sharp bound $2Δ-1$ for every $Δ\ge 6$, settling the remaining cases. The proof uses discharging; the case $Δ=6$ is computer-assisted.
comment: 21 pages. Ancillary files contain the certificates and verification scripts for the computer-assisted case of maximum degree 6

title: The Number of Polytope Trees and Beyond
summary: We study the symmetry-weighted enumeration of complexes formed by gluing copies of a regular polytope. For polytope trees and complexes obtained by attaching such trees to a fixed initial complex, we derive cut-and-join recurrences, differential equations for generating functions, explicit counting formulas, and asymptotic estimates. We then extend the method to complexes with cycles in their dual graphs, enumerating them by the numbers of polytopes and free facets. We derive recurrence relations and partial differential equations for the corresponding bivariate generating functions. In this setting, we obtain recurrences for connected configurations and explicit coefficient formulas for possibly disconnected configurations, both with and without a distinguished initial complex.

title: A quasi-polynomial $χ$-bound for $P_6$-free graphs
summary: In this paper we prove that every graph $G$ with no induced six-vertex path satisfies $χ(G)\le ω(G)^{c\log_2ω(G)}$ for $c=45/\log_2(4/3)<109$. The best previous bound was exponential in $ω(G)$. Our result is the first quasi-polynomial bound for $P_6$-free graphs and generalizes the bound for $P_5$-free graphs by Scott, Seymour, and Spirkl [Polynomial bounds for chromatic number. {IV}. {A} near-polynomial bound for excluding the five-vertex path. {\em Combinatorica}, 43(5):845--852, 2023].

title: An exact compression-and-lifting procedure and D-optimal designs of orders 198 and 170
summary: We develop a compression-and-lifting procedure for constructing D-optimal complementary pairs on finite abelian groups of odd order. The procedure separates the Fourier conditions preserved by compression from those needed to recover the original binary sequences. For groups with a cyclic factor of order nine, integer matching conditions separate compatible classes of local sign assignments. Their exact sizes can be computed before full sequences are generated, allowing searches to discard incompatible pairs and select manageable classes. A bound on cosets on which a sequence is constant also excludes certain automorphisms as fixing symmetries. Applying the method yields supplementary difference sets with parameters $(99;43,42;36)$ and $(85;39,34;31)$, resolving two previously undecided parameter sets. These give the first D-optimal matrix of order $198$ and constructions with new parameters at the known order $170$. For the successful length-$99$ compression, the exact class condition removes $99.9888\%$ of candidate pairs while preserving every D-optimal lift. A reflection-invariant construction at length $85$ gives seven supplementary difference set classes and fourteen matrix classes under signed row and column permutations, paired by transposition. The class reductions guide computation; finding suitable compressions and matching their lifts remain search problems.

title: Searching for binary orientable sequences
summary: An aperiodic binary orientable sequence is a finite sequence of zeros and ones for which, for some integer $n$, all the subsequences of $n$ consecutive symbols, read either forwards or backwards, are distinct. Analogously, a periodic binary orientable sequence is an infinite periodic sequence of zeros and ones for which, for some integer $n$, all the subsequences of $n$ consecutive symbols, read either forwards or backwards, are distinct within a single period of the sequence. Such sequences have potential application in position-location applications. For applications, the longer the sequence (or the greater the period in the periodic case) the greater its utility, but yet while constructions are known for such sequences, and upper bounds on their length (or period) exist, the precise maximum length (or period) was previously unknown for anything other than small values of $n$. In this note the results of LLM-conducted searches for the longest possible aperiodic and periodic binary orientable sequences for $n\leq16$ are reported. In each case an example of a sequence of the maximum discovered length is also provided, and the maximum possible length is now determined for every $n\leq16$ for both the periodic and aperiodic cases.

title: Extremal diagonal-coherent binary codes: shortened Hamming cores, deep holes, and the 64 I-Ching hexagrams
summary: Each of the 64 hexagrams of the I-Ching, or Book of Changes, is a stack of six Yin-Yang lines and is therefore a binary vector of length 6; the eight hexagrams formed by repeating a single trigram span a doubled-trigram subspace $Δ$. We ask which binary $[6,3,3]$ codes are compatible with this trigram structure. We show that a $[6,3,3]$ code meets $Δ$ in at most four codewords, that the four are then forced to be the doubled trigrams Earth, Fire, Wind and Lake, and that exactly two codes attain this bound: the shortened Hamming code $\mathcal C_A$ and its dual. Since $\mathcal C_A$ has covering radius 2, its eight codewords, their radius-one balls, and its eight deep holes together reconstruct all 64 hexagrams. In general, we call a binary code of length $2m$ with $d \ge 3$ diagonal-coherent if it contains the half of the diagonal subspace $\{(u,u)\}$ coming from even-weight vectors $u$ -- the largest part of that subspace a single-error-correcting code can contain -- and extremal if its dimension is as large as possible. For $m\ge2$ and $r=\lceil\log_2(2m+1)\rceil$, we determine the number $N(m)$ of extremal diagonal-coherent codes with parameters $[\,2m,\ 2m-r,\ \ge3\,]$, show that diagonal coherence entails no loss of redundancy, and determine their minimum distances. We also put these codes in a normal form, determine their hulls, and show that each has covering radius $2$ with exactly $2^r-1-2m$ deep-hole cosets. Finally we propose three open problems.

title: The chromatic number of a random graph with $o(n^{3/2})$ edges
summary: Let $G(n,m)$ be the Erdos-Renyi random graph with $n$ vertices and $m$ edges and let $δ>0$. Alon and Krivelevich [Combinatorica 1997] proved that for any sequence $m\leq n^{3/2-δ}$ there \emph{exists} an integer sequence $q=q(n)$ such that the chromatic number of $G(n,m)$ equals either $q$ or $q+1$ with probability tending to one as $n\to\infty$. In this paper, we give an explicit formula for this sequence $q(n)$ and confirm their result under a less restrictive assumption that $m=o(n^{3/2})$. Furthermore, we show that for all but a vanishing proportion of the admissible values of $m$, the chromatic number of $G(n,m)$ equals $q$ with high probability.

title: Noninteger completely monotonic degrees of Stirling remainders and their derivatives
summary: For Stirling expansions truncated after at least two Bernoulli terms, we disprove the three real-degree conjectures recorded by Mahmoud and Qi for the signed remainders of the logarithm of the gamma function and their derivatives. We give a unified proof of the corresponding integer-degree formula, recovering known cases and resolving Zhu's conjectures for higher derivatives in this range. Every real completely monotonic degree lies strictly between the predicted integer and the next integer. We obtain a universal fractional lower bound through an explicit inverse function and a simpler rational bound valid for every derivative order. A local estimate for the negative part of the Laplace kernel's derivative with respect to its logarithmic variable makes the lower improvement proportional to the reciprocal of the combined truncation and derivative order. Together with a uniform upper bound, this determines the exact order of decay of the fractional excess for each fixed derivative order and for its supremum over all derivative orders. Sharper kernel estimates give stronger bounds for the first two degrees. The proof combines fractional positivity criteria, the classical Laplace representation, a sign characterization of the associated densities, and a convexity obstruction at the upper integer endpoint. All estimates used in the proofs are analytic. The exact real degrees and the optimal asymptotic constants remain open.

title: Combinatorial models for Quasicrystals and Schur-Weyl Duality
summary: Quasicrystals were defined by Cain and Malheiro and Maas-Gariépy to model the decomposition of Schur polynomials into fundamental quasisymmetric functions. We define a new combinatorial model for crystal graphs of type $A_{n-1}$, called parsed content words, for which the decomposition into quasicrystals is particularly evident. We use the model to describe a combinatorial interpretation of Schur-Weyl duality and recover the classical combinatorial proof of the well-known expansion of homogeneous symmetric functions into Schur functions within our framework.

title: Inequalities and asymptotics for hook numbers in two partition functions of MacMahon and Andrews
summary: Motivated by recent studies of hook length biases in restricted partitions, we investigate the total number of hooks of fixed length in two partition functions introduced by MacMahon and Andrews. In $1916$, MacMahon proved that the number of partitions of $n$ in which no part appears with multiplicity one equals the number of partitions of $n$ into parts that are even or congruent to $3 \pmod{6}$. For a positive integer $r$, let $A_r(n)$ count the partitions of $n$ in which every part occurring an odd number of times occurs at least $2r+1$ times, and let $B_r(n)$ count the partitions into parts that are even or congruent to $2r+1 \pmod{4r+2}$. Andrews proved that $A_r(n)=B_r(n)$ for all positive integers $r$ and nonnegative integers $n$, thereby recovering MacMahon's identity as the special case $r=1$. We derive generating functions and asymptotic formulas for the total numbers of hooks of lengths $1$, $2$, and $3$ in both partition classes, employing Wright's circle method. These asymptotic formulas yield several hook length bias results. In particular, for sufficiently large $n$, the $B_r$-type partitions exhibit more $1$-hooks than the $A_r$-type partitions, whereas for hook lengths $2$ and $3$, the bias is reversed when $r=1$ and favors the $B_r$-type partitions when $r\geq 2$. We also establish asymptotic inequalities among hook numbers of different lengths within each partition class. Finally, for fixed hook lengths $\ell\in\{1,2,3\}$, we prove that the $B_r$-type partitions exhibit more $\ell$-hooks than the $B_{r+1}$-type partitions for sufficiently large $n$. These results reveal systematic asymptotic patterns in the distribution of small hook lengths across the two partition families.

title: Packing colourings of claw-free subcubic graphs
summary: We prove that every claw-free subcubic graph admits a \packA-packing colouring, confirming a conjecture of Mortada, El Zein and Al Hajjar. The proof combines a reduction to line graphs of subdivided loopless cubic multigraphs with local colouring extensions. We also give a negative answer to their question on \packB-packing colourings by constructing an infinite family of connected bridgeless claw-free cubic counterexamples. The smallest graph in this family has 36 vertices. More generally, we characterise the simple cubic graphs whose triangle expansions admit a \packB-packing colouring in terms of gated independent odd-cycle transversals. This characterisation gives a classification for connected bridgeless claw-free cubic bases and shows that the double triangle expansion of a loopless cubic multigraph admits such a colouring if and only if the multigraph has a perfect matching.

title: Solving Large SDPs from Flag Algebra Problems
summary: The flag algebra method is a general tool in extremal combinatorics, which has been useful in tackling open problems concerning graphs, hypergraphs, permutations, point sets, and other structures. The method establishes combinatorial inequalities via sums of squares, which are usually obtained by a semidefinite relaxation of the original combinatorial problem. A typical application of the method in graph theory starts with fixing a parameter $n$ followed by constructing a semidefinite program based on the (subgraph) structure of all $n$-vertex graphs. In the standard formulation before symmetry reductions, there is a coefficient constraint for every admissible $n$-vertex graph up to isomorphism. For 3-uniform hypergraphs, there are 2,136 of them on 6 vertices and 7,013,320 on 7 vertices. While solving the resulting program for $n=6$ is an easy task on any modern computer, the programs for $n = 7$ seems out of reach, mainly because the SDP solvers need too much RAM. Yet solving such programs for as large $n$ as possible is desirable because they typically yield better bounds for the original combinatorial problems. We bypass the aforementioned memory requirements by linear programming with cutting planes. Although we do not guarantee that this cutting-plane procedure reaches an optimum in finitely many iterations, in many flag algebra instances it uses much less memory and yields improved bounds for well-known hypergraph Turán problems. We use this method to obtain numerical bounds for Turán densities and codegree squared densities of several 3-uniform hypergraphs including the tetrahedron, where we obtained the upper bound 0.55753 and tetrahedron without one edge with a new upper bound 0.2865. It also allows to tackle bounds on Turán densities of 7-vertex 3-graphs using flag algebras, which was not possible before.

title: Between the Semi-Random Process and G(n,p)
summary: We study a random graph process that connects the Erdős--Rényi random graph with the semi-random process. In each round, a uniformly random vertex is revealed together with a uniformly random candidate set of $s$ possible partners, and Builder chooses one of them. We study how this limited adaptivity $s$ changes the hitting times of monotone graph properties and how the familiar logarithmic ``coupon--collector'' delays in random graphs are reflected in this setting.

title: On Lewis's homotopy in distance-regular graphs
summary: In 2000, Lewis introduced a nested sequence of normal subgroups of the fundamental group of a distance-regular graph $Γ$. While the full homotopy group itself is simply a free group, it is interesting to determine the smallest integer $k$ such that every closed walk in $Γ$ can be built, up to homotopy, from closed walks of "essential length" $k$ or less. Lewis proved that $k\le 6$ for any $Q$-polynomial distance-regular graph $Γ$ that is not a pseudoquotient. In this paper, we prove that $k=3$ for Johnson graphs and that $k=4$ in the case of Hamming graphs. We also compute the homotopy groups of natural cell complexes associated to the folded Johnson graphs and folded cubes. The paper finishes with some open questions and suggestions for further lines of investigation.

title: Improved Bounds on Proportional Choice Numbers
summary: Proportional choosability is a list analogue of equitable coloring introduced in 2019 that imposes both upper and lower bounds on color class sizes based on the availability of each color. The proportional choice number of a graph $G$, denoted by $χ_{pc}(G)$, is the smallest positive integer $k$ such that $G$ is proportionally $k$-choosable. We consider two previously posed questions regarding proportional choice numbers: (1) Is there a constant $C$ such that $χ_{pc}(P_n) \leq C$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$? and (2) Is it the case that for any graph $G$, $χ_{pc}(G) \leq Δ(G)+1$ where $Δ(G)$ is the maximum degree of $G$? In this paper we answer both questions: the first in the affirmative and the second in the negative. Specifically, we prove that $χ_{pc}(G) \leq 2^{χ'(G)}$ for every graph $G$ where $χ'(G)$ is the chromatic index of $G$. Consequently, $χ_{pc}(P_n) \leq 4$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$. We also prove that when $G$ is the disjoint union of $(a+b-1)$ copies of $K_{a,b}$, $χ_{pc}(G)=a+b$. In particular, for each $m \in \mathbb{N}$, there is a graph $G$ with $Δ(G)=m$ and $χ_{pc}(G)=2Δ(G)$.

title: Nilpotent Lie algebras of nilpotence class at most three via graphs
summary: In this work, we associate with each finite simple graph $G$ a nilpotent Lie algebra $\mathfrak{n}_G$ of class at most three, whose underlying vector space has a basis indexed by the vertices, edges, and paths of length two of $G$. Its nilpotency class is exactly three if and only if $G$ contains a path of length two. We compute the dimensions of its lower central series and describe its center. Over fields of characteristic different from two, we prove that two such Lie algebras are isomorphic if and only if their underlying graphs are isomorphic. We also give an algebraic description using quotients involving exterior and symmetric squares. Finally, we study balanced blow-ups and prove that $\mathfrak{n}_G$ is a retract of $\mathfrak{n}_{G^{(m)}}$.

title: Explicit weighing matrices $W(n,k)$ for all $n \equiv 0 \pmod 4$ with $4 \le n \le 108$, and all $1 \le k \le n$
summary: We present an explicit weighing matrix $W(n,k)$ for every order $n\equiv 0\pmod 4$ with $4\le n\le 108$ and every weight $1\le k\le n$: 1512 matrices in total, each checked in exact integer arithmetic. Of these, 961 come from classical constructions (identity, direct sums, Kronecker products, Paley matrices and skew-Hadamard doubling) and 551 are Goethals-Seidel matrices, found by exhaustive search (24 matrices, $n\le 24$) or by simulated annealing on the periodic autocorrelation cost (527 matrices, $n\ge 28$). The note is self-contained as far as the methods are concerned: it presents all the construction methods used and the algorithm that selects among them, explains the algorithm step by step, proves every identity on which the constructions rely, and illustrates each method with a matrix taken from the catalogue. It does not reproduce the 1512 matrices, which are available in the repository. It also gives a short parity obstruction to Goethals-Seidel matrices $W(4m,4m-1)$ with $m$ even, and lists the generating sequences of thirteen matrices whose parameters appear as unresolved in historical tables consulted by the author; their status in the current literature is still being checked, and no claim of priority is made.
comment: 32 pages. Code and data: https://github.com/adrianmaciasquintero/weighing-matrices (archived at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23484194)

title: Extremal 3-uniform hypergraphs without generalized 4-cycles
summary: Let $f_r(n)$ be the maximum number of edges in an $n$-vertex $r$-uniform hypergraph in which all disjoint pairs of edges have distinct unions. In 1977, Erdős posed the problem of determining $f_r(n)$ and, in particular, asked whether $f_3(n)=O(n^2)$. Füredi later proved that $\binom{n-1}{r-1}+\left\lfloor (n-1)/r\right\rfloor \le f_r(n)<\frac72\binom{n}{r-1}$ for $r\ge3$ and $n\ge2r$. Motivated by his constructions, he further conjectured that $f_3(n)\le\binom{n}{2}$ for all sufficiently large $n$, and that, for each fixed $r\ge4$, the lower bound is exact for all sufficiently large $n$. This is known as the Erdős--Füredi conjecture. In a recent breakthrough, Huang, Ma and Yang proved the conjecture for every fixed $r\ge4$ and characterized all extremal hypergraphs. In this paper, we settle the remaining $3$-uniform case for every $n$. The bound is sharp whenever $n\ge5$ and $n\equiv1,5\pmod{20}$. Our proof uses a local weight inequality and a transfer argument.

title: Spectral Turán problems for complete bipartite expansions in linear hypergraphs
summary: An $r$-uniform hypergraph is linear if any two edges share at most one vertex. For a family $\mathcal F$ of $r$-graphs, let $\text{ex}^{\text{lin}}_r(n,\mathcal F)$ and $\text{spex}^{\text{lin}}_r(n,\mathcal F)$ denote, respectively, the maximum number of edges and the maximum spectral radius of an $n$-vertex $\mathcal F$-free linear $r$-graph. In this paper, we show that for $t\ge s\ge3$, $\text{spex}^{\text{lin}}_r(n,K_{s,t}^{+})\le \frac{(t-s+1)^{1/s}}{r-1}n^{1-1/s}+o(n^{1-1/s})$, where $K_{s,t}^{+}$ is the $r$-graph obtained from the complete bipartite graph $K_{s,t}$ by enlarging each edge with $r-2$ new vertices. This answers a problem of She, Fan and Kang in a stronger form. Moreover, our result implies that $\text{ex}^\text{lin}_r(n,K_{s,t}^{+}) \le \frac{(t-s+1)^{1/s}}{r(r-1)}n^{2-1/s}+o(n^{2-1/s})$, which improves the leading coefficient in the corresponding bound of Gao and Chang. We also give a construction which implies that $\text{spex}^{\text{lin}}_r(n,K_{s,t}^{+})=Θ(n^{1-1/s})$ and $\text{ex}^\text{lin}_r(n,K_{s,t}^{+})=Θ(n^{2-1/s})$ for $s\ge 4r-6$ and $t>(s-1)!$.

title: Minimum Distance Spectral Radius of Tree with Given Maximum Degree
summary: In this article, the unique graph with minimum distance spectral radius among trees with given order $n$ and maximum degree $\varDelta$ is determined, where $2\varDelta+1 \leq n \leq \varDelta^{2} +1$ for $\varDelta \geq 3$. This article is a part proof of the conjecture proposed in $\cite{ref1}$.

title: A planar signed graph with circular chromatic number five
summary: A circular $r$-coloring of a signed graph maps its vertices to a circle of circumference $r\ge2$, with the endpoints of negative edges at circular distance at least $1$ and those of positive edges at most $r/2-1$; the circular chromatic number is the infimum of such $r$. We construct a simple planar signed triangulation on $85$ vertices with circular chromatic number exactly $5$. This improves the lower bound on the supremum of the circular chromatic numbers of simple planar signed graphs from $14/3$ to $5$, giving a partial answer to a question posed by Naserasr, Wang, and Zhu.

title: Colored Partitions and Minimal Excludants
summary: In this article, we introduce the concept of minimal excludants in colored partitions and extend it to the framework of least $r$-gaps. In particular, we focus on $k$-colored partitions and cubic partitions, deriving the generating functions for the sums of minimal excludants and least $r$-gaps, and analyzing their asymptotic behaviors. Notably, the presented theory is comprehensively extended by the systematic generalization of each result for minimal excludants in $k$-colored partitions to the case of least $r$-gaps. We introduce generalized cubic partitions and discover the minimal excludant, as well as several additional results.

title: The \(\mathcal A_α\)-Spectral Turán Problem for \(s\)-Clique Tensors of \(K_{r+1}\)-Free Graphs
summary: For fixed $r\geq3$ and $0<α<1$, we study the maximum $α$-$s$-clique spectral radius among $n$-vertex $K_{r+1}$-free graphs. Here $\mathcal A_{α,s}(G)=α\mathcal D_s(G)+(1-α)\mathcal A_s(G)$, where $\mathcal A_s(G)$ and $\mathcal D_s(G)$ are the adjacency and degree tensors of the $s$-clique hypergraph of $G$. For $s=r$, put $c_r=((r-1)/r)^{r-1}$. We prove that, for all sufficiently large $n$, the unique extremal graph is the Turán graph $T_r(n)$ if $α\leq c_r$, and $K_1\vee T_{r-1}(n-1)$ if $α>c_r$. For general $3\leq s\leq r$ and $n\geq r$, every extremal graph is complete $r$-partite. The asymptotic maximum $α$-$r$-clique spectral radius among $n$-vertex $K_{r+1}$-free graphs is $\max\{r^{1-r},α(r-1)^{1-r}\}n^{r-1}+o(n^{r-1})$. In every asymptotically extremal sequence of complete $r$-partite graphs, all parts have size $n/r+o(n)$ when $α<c_r$; when $α>c_r$, one part has size $o(n)$ and the remaining parts have size $n/(r-1)+o(n)$. At $α=c_r$, both part-size patterns are asymptotically extremal.

title: General-position sets and linear hypergraphs
summary: We prove that every linear hypergraph on $N$ vertices with edge sizes $O(\sqrt N)$ and $O(N^2\log N)$ triples contained in its edges has a subset of size $Ω(\sqrt N)$ meeting each edge in at most two vertices. As an application, every set of $N$ planar points with at most $\sqrt N$ collinear points contains $Ω(\sqrt N)$ points in general position. This proves a conjecture of Payne and Wood and gives the optimal quadratic bound for a geometric Ramsey problem posed by Gowers.

title: The Golomb--Welch conjecture for arbitrary centre sets
summary: We prove that for all $n\ge3$ and $r\ge2$, the Lee ball $B_n(r)$ does not tile $\Z^n$ by translations, resolving the Golomb--Welch conjecture for arbitrary centre sets and completing the existence classification of perfect Lee codes in $\Z^n$. The proof combines translation-invariant averaging, boundary contact identities, and integer moment inequalities with coefficient comparisons in stable symmetric functions. Consequently, we obtain finite local obstructions, strict Banach density gaps for packings and coverings, and the nonexistence of exact measurable Lee-ball towers. In the lattice specialization, our result classifies the attainability of the Lee bound for even-degree abelian Cayley graphs, excludes normal topological coverings and Galois graph coverings for Lee-ball completions, and gives a strict node bound for lattice cubature as well as the nonexistence of subgroup-indexed orthogonal exponential bases on $B_n(r)$.

title: Sharp bounds for Duke--Erdős--Rödl problems on cycle-connected subgraphs
summary: For $k\ge2$, a graph is $C_{2k}$-connected if every two distinct edges lie together on an even cycle of length at most $2k$ in that graph. Let $f_k(n,m)$ be the largest number of edges in a $C_{2k}$-connected subgraph that every $n$-vertex graph with $m$ edges must contain. In this paper, we study two cycle-connected problems raised by Duke, Erdős and Rödl. First, Duke, Erdős and Rödl showed that $f_3(n,\lfloor n^{2-β}\rfloor)=Θ(n^{2-3β})$ for every fixed $0< β<1/2$ and ask for the case of $β\ge 1/2$. We solve this problem in a stronger form by determining that the optimal range of $β$ is $(0,2/3]$. Second, we prove that $f_2(n,\binom n2-s)=(1/(2e)+o(1))n^3/s$ whenever $\frac{s}{n}\to\infty$ and $s=o(n^2)$, determining the leading constant in an estimate of Duke, Erdős, and Rödl. The first result uses a finite-field construction and a count of three-edge paths. The second uses the known structure of $C_4$-connected graphs and estimates for complete bipartite subgraphs in a random graph.

title: On first-order limiting probabilities for small permutation classes
summary: Given a small permutation class $\mathcal{P}$, we consider the set of possible limits of the probability $\mathbb{P}\big(\mathbfσ_n \models Ψ\big)$ that a uniformly chosen random permutation $\mathbfσ_n\in \mathcal{P}_n$ satisfies a fixed first-order sentence in Theory of Two Orders (TOTO). In the case of small permutation classes with polynomial growth, we show this limit set is finite, and characterize the set explicitly. In particular, we prove that many natural small permutation classes of polynomial growth arising from permutation matrices satisfy a $0$-$1$ convergence law, and have an infinite model. In the case of small permutation classes with exponential growth we show that the limit set is dense in $[0,1]$, thereby extending a result of Albert--Bouvel--Féray--Noy, using different methods, to this range.

title: A general algebraic characterization of extremal $Δ$-trees and $k$-cyclic graphs for degree-homogeneous VDB indices
summary: We present a general algebraic method for maximizing a vertex-degree-based (VDB) topological index $TI(G) = \sum_{uv \in E(G)} f(d(u),d(v))$ over the class of $n$-vertex trees with a prescribed maximum degree $Δ\ge 3$. By expressing the edge multiplicities of the basis $\mathcal{B} = \{(1,Δ), (Δ,Δ)\}$ via degree-sum identities, we reduce the maximization of $TI(T)$ to the minimization of an explicit discrete penalty function $G(x,y)$ over the non-basic edges. We formulate five analytical conditions on the weight function $f(x,y)$ that dictate the optimal edge distributions, yielding a complete characterization of the extremal trees across all congruence classes of $n \pmod{Δ- 1}$. Additionally, we provide their explicit construction by attaching leaves to a core of internal vertices. Applying this framework, we obtain the complete characterization of extremal $Δ$-trees for the Degree-Ratio Sombor ($DRSO$), Symmetric Division Deg ($SDD$), and Hyperbolic Sombor ($HSO$) indices for all $Δ\ge 3$. Furthermore, the analytical conditions identify the exact degree thresholds for the Arithmetic-Geometric ($AG$) and Diminished Sombor ($DSO$) indices, showing that the same extremal family maximizes $AG$ if and only if $3 \le Δ\le 8$, and $DSO$ if and only if $3 \le Δ\le 4$. Finally, since changing the edge count from $m = n - 1$ to $m = n - 1 + k$ affects only the constant term in the decomposition while leaving the penalty function $G(x,y)$ invariant, the method extends directly to connected $k$-cyclic graphs.

title: Counting Admissible Sets of Integers: A Proof of the Erdős--Nicolas--Sárközy Conjecture
summary: A finite set of positive integers is admissible if any two of its subsets with the same sum have the same cardinality. In 1991, Erdős, Nicolas and Sárközy conjectured that $\log a(N)\asymp\sqrt N$, where $a(N)$ denotes the number of nonempty admissible subsets of $\{1,\ldots,N\}$. We prove this conjecture by showing that there are absolute constants $c,C>0$ such that $\exp(c\sqrt N)\le a(N)\le\exp(C\sqrt N)$ for every integer $N\ge4$. The same bounds hold for the number of admissible sets with maximum $N$. For the upper bound, we show that every sufficiently large admissible set $A\subseteq\{1,\ldots,N\}$ contains a subset of proportional size whose doubling constant is $O(N/|A|^2)$.

title: The Plane-Saturation Ratio of Planar Graphs
summary: For a planar graph \(G\), a plane subgraph \(H\) is plane-saturated with respect to \(G\) if adding any edge to the fixed drawing of \(H\), possibly together with new vertices, either creates a crossing or results in a graph that is not a subgraph of \(G\). The plane-saturation ratio \(\psr(G)\) is the minimum of \(e(H)/e(G)\) over all plane-saturated subgraphs \(H\) of \(G\). For nonnegative integers \(k_1\) and \(k_2\), let \(\cG_{k_1,k_2}\) denote the class of planar graphs in which, for each \(i\in\{1,2\}\), at most \(k_i\) vertices of degree \(i\) have any prescribed neighborhood, where \(k_i=0\) means that vertices of degree \(i\) are forbidden. We prove that every \(G\in\cG_{k_1,k_2}\) with at least one edge satisfies $\psr(G)>\frac{1}{9+k_1+6k_2}.$ This settles two conjectures of Clifton and Salia.

title: Graham's rearrangement conjecture in finite abelian groups
summary: Graham conjectured in 1971 that every subset of the nonzero elements of a prime cyclic group admits an ordering with pairwise distinct nonempty partial sums. Recently, the work of Pham and Sauermann, together with earlier results, settled this conjecture for all sufficiently large primes. In this paper, we prove that there is an absolute integer $n_0$ such that every subset $S\subseteq G\setminus\{0\}$ of a finite abelian group with $|S|\ge n_0$ admits such an ordering, which also solves a conjecture of Alspach and Liversidge for all sufficiently large sets. A key ingredient of our proof is a sufficient condition via additive dimension: If $|S|=n$ and $S$ contains a dissociated subset of size at least $Ω((\log n)^2/\log\log n)$, then $S$ has an ordering in which no proper nonempty interval of consecutive terms sums to zero. This bound is within a factor of $O(\log n/\log\log n)$ of the smallest possible additive dimension of an $n$-element set.

title: Proof of the Harary--Hill conjecture: an exposition
summary: The Harary--Hill conjecture states that the crossing number of the complete graph $K_n$ is exactly $\frac{1}{4}\left\lfloor\frac{n}{2}\right\rfloor \left\lfloor\frac{n-1}{2}\right\rfloor \left\lfloor\frac{n-2}{2}\right\rfloor \left\lfloor\frac{n-3}{2}\right\rfloor$. We present a streamlined variant of the proof of this conjecture recently announced by OpenAI (2026). Although the original proof is relatively short, it is quite difficult to follow. We simplify several steps and provide a concise and accessible exposition of the proof. We also combine this new result with known reductions to determine the crossing numbers of several other graph families.

title: A graded version of the separator theorem for planar graphs
summary: We prove that every planar graph on $n$ vertices has a vertex ordering $v_1,v_2,\ldots,v_n$ in which each prefix $\{v_1,\ldots,v_i\}$ is joined to at most $C\sqrt{i}$ elements of $\{v_{i+1},\ldots,v_n\}$, where $C$ is an absolute constant. Consequently, every prefix can be separated from its complement by deleting $O\left(\sqrt{i}\right)$ vertices lying entirely in its complement.

title: Dual near-factorizations and Schur products in association schemes
summary: Let $G$ and $H$ be Gram matrices of spherical $2$-designs on the same number of indices. We study when their Schur product is again the Gram matrix of a spherical design. We give a criterion in terms of orthogonal projections with constant diagonal, and an explicit $15$-point spherical $3$-design whose Gram matrix belongs to no symmetric Bose-Mesner algebra. For a symmetric association scheme, the factorization problem takes the form $v(E_S\circ E_T)=μE_U$. This is a counterpart of ordinary matrix product factorizations in the adjacency basis. The case $E_U=I-E_0$ gives a dual near-factorization and has a regular simplex as its normalized output. We characterize complementary input supports by a strongly regular fusion, give a reciprocal criterion, and classify the case in which one factor is the last Hamming idempotent.

title: A proof of the Grothendieck join-meet positivity
summary: We prove the (signed) Grothendieck join--meet positivity $$ G_{λ\veeμ}G_{λ\wedgeμ} -G_λG_μ\in \sum_ν \mathbb{N}\cdot (-1)^{|ν|-|λ|-|μ|}G_ν$$ for stable Grothendieck polynomials using geometric Satake equivalence, thereby resolving a conjecture posed by Thomas and Yong.

title: The $e$-expansion of integral form Macdonald polynomials
summary: In this paper, we investigate the expansion of the integral form Macdonald polynomials $J_μ(x;q,t)$ in the elementary symmetric function basis. Motivated by the connection between chromatic symmetric functions and LLT polynomials, we conjecture the $e$-positivity of a normalization of $J_μ(x;q,t)$. We verify the conjecture when $μ$ is either a hook or a two-column partition. In the hook case, we express the $e$-coefficients as weighted sums over compositions. In the two-column case, we derive explicit formulas for the $e$-coefficients.

title: On strong odd colorings of sparse graphs
summary: A strong odd coloring of a graph is a proper vertex coloring such that for every vertex $v$, each color appearing on the neighborhood of $v$ appears an odd number of times. We investigate strong odd colorings of sparse graphs, where sparsity of a graph $G$ is measured in terms of maximum average degree, denoted $\operatorname{mad}(G)$. We prove that the optimal threshold on the maximum average degree guaranteeing a strong odd $c$-coloring is $4-Θ(\frac{1}{c})$ as $c\to\infty$. Moreover, for every $c\geq 5$, this threshold is strictly smaller than the threshold for odd $c$-coloring. We also determine the sharp threshold on the maximum average degree guaranteeing a strong odd $5$-coloring: every graph $G$ with $\operatorname{mad}(G)<\frac{7}{3}$ has a strong odd $5$-coloring, and this bound is sharp. In addition, we show that every graph $G$ with $\operatorname{mad}(G)<\frac{11}{5}$ and no induced $5$-cycle has a strong odd $4$-coloring. Note that the $5$-cycle has maximum average degree 2 and no strong odd $4$-coloring.

title: Rainbow maps and the number of graceful labelings of trees
summary: Let $τ(N)$ be the number of graceful labelings of trees with $N$ edges, that is, the number of spanning trees of the complete graph on $\{0,1,\dots,N\}$ whose edges have distinct lengths. The answer to exercise 7.2.2.3-106 of The Art of Computer Programming states that, if an empirical observation of Anick is true, then $τ(n)=\exp(n\ln n-n\ln(e/b)+O(\log n))$ with $b\approx0.636$, and that rigorous proofs are unknown. We prove that $|\logτ(N)-(N\log N-N\log(e/b))|\le152(1+\log(N+1))^4$ for every $N\ge3$, with $b=2/π$. A rainbow map of order $N$ sends each vertex $k\in\{1,\dots,N-1\}$ to a vertex $f(k)\in\{0,\dots,N\}$ so that the lengths $|f(k)-k|$ are $1,\dots,N-1$ in some order. Acyclic rainbow maps are exactly the graceful labelings, and all rainbow maps are counted by the Whitty numbers $W(N)$ (OEIS A134983). We show that $τ(N)\le W(N)\leτ(N)e^{151(1+\log(N+1))^4}$ by a combinatorial argument: for fixed directions, rainbow maps are rook placements on a Ferrers board; a swap injection shows that a uniformly random rainbow map has $O(\log^2N)$ cycles on average; and an inequality on the periods of a word shows that the $c$ cycles of a rainbow map can be removed by changing $O(c\log N)$ edges. We also show that $W(N)$ is the total weight of a family of weighted Motzkin paths. This yields exact enumerations, an alternating sum for $W(N)$, and a representation of $W(N)$ as a moment of a continuous dual Hahn weight, from which $|\log W(N)-(N\log(2N/π)-N)|\le5(1+\log(N+1))$. The main theorem has been formalized in Lean 4; its combinatorial half uses no axioms beyond those of Lean.
comment: 27 pages, 2 figures. A Lean 4 formalization of the main theorem is included in the ancillary files (directory anc/lean)

title: Cross work induced by transformations on the symmetric group and related transformation semigroups
summary: We introduce a new permutation statistic, called the \emph{cross work}, on four important subsemigroups of the partial transformation semigroup $\mathcal{PT}_n$: the symmetric group $\mathcal{S}_n$, the semigroup of singular transformations $\mathrm{Sing}_n$, the symmetric inverse semigroup $\mathcal{I}_n$, and the semigroup $\mathcal{POI}_n$ of partial order-preserving injective transformations. The cross work is defined via local distance interactions between adjacent positions and their images. Fundamental invariance properties are established, including inversion invariance under a natural symmetry condition and a characterization of conjugations preserving the statistic. Using elementary combinatorial methods, we derive closed formulas for the total and average cross work on $\mathcal{S}_n$. We also determine the exact minimum and maximum values of the cross work, showing that the maximal value grows quadratically with $n$.
comment: 20 pages. An article by Nsibiet E. Udo, Victor A. Owai and Moses O. Francis

title: The maximum spectral radius of connected graphs with prescribed order and size
summary: In 1986, Brualdi and Solheid asked which connected graph of prescribed order and size has maximum adjacency spectral radius. We complete the classification for every feasible pair of parameters. We prove that no graph outside the dense and star threshold families is extremal, including at ties, and settle the range $n\le e+1$, where the star candidate is not defined. The final comparison \emph{between} the dense and star candidates is supplied by Damnjanović's Propositions~4.1--4.2, not reproved here. We combine an exact Bellman recursion with dense-core domination, fractional complete-split bounds, and a virtual-star inequality. Three remaining comparison families (J), (K1), and (K2) are established analytically and by exact polynomial and Sturm certificates. The exact certificates are implemented in Python/SymPy and SageMath.
comment: 45 pages, includes computer-assisted proofs and supplementary Python/SageMath verification programs

title: On the product of nontrivial cross-intersecting families
summary: Let $n\geq2\ell\geq2k\geq6$ and $n>k+\ell$. We determine the maximum of $|\mathcal A||\mathcal B|$ over all nonempty, nontrivial cross-intersecting families $\mathcal A\subseteq\binom{[n]}k$ and $\mathcal B\subseteq\binom{[n]}\ell$. The exact bound is $|\mathcal A||\mathcal B|\leq\max\{M_1,M_2\}$, where \[ \begin{aligned} M_1 &=\left(\binom{n-1}{k-1}-\binom{n-\ell-1}{k-1}+1\right) \left(\binom{n-1}{\ell-1}-\binom{n-k-1}{\ell-1}+1\right),\\ M_2 &=\left(\binom{n-2}{\ell-2}+1\right) \sum_{i=1}^{2} \left(\binom{n-i}{k-1}-\binom{n-\ell-i}{k-1}\right). \end{aligned} \] Both terms are attained by explicit constructions: a Hilton--Milner-type pair and a two-point construction, respectively. We classify all equality cases, including the additional cross-triangle pairs when $k=\ell=3$. Two structural results underlie the proof. First, we establish a restricted-lex comparison theorem showing that restricted lexicographic initial segments minimize disjointness neighborhoods, and characterize equality at the first nontrivial threshold. Second, a decomposition of critically shifted families into two parts with disjoint cores leads to a sharp product theorem, with equality characterized, for all cross-intersecting pairs admitting this decomposition, without additional nontriviality assumptions. Endpoint comparisons and reverse shifting complete the proof for unequal as well as equal uniformities.

title: The flag major index on conjugacy classes of wreath products
summary: A classical result, independently proved by Garsia and by Wachs, gives a simple and elegant closed expression for the evaluation, at a primitive root of unity, of the major index generating function over a conjugacy class in the symmetric group. In this paper, we generalize this result to the flag major index generating function over conjugacy classes in any wreath product $\mathbb{Z}_{r}\wr S_{n}$. Our approach is new, and applies conjugation by a Coxeter element as a cyclic group action on the conjugacy class. This leads to a simple formula in the general case.

title: Upper bounding the coefficients of Tutte polynomials with a variable fixed
summary: The Tutte polynomial is a fundamental invariant of graphs and matroids. For a matroid M of rank r, the Tutte polynomial T_M(x,y) of M serves as a generalization of the characteristic polynomial chi_M(x), with the relationship given by chi_M(x) = (-1)^r T_M(1-x,0). For any real number t satisfying 0 <= t <= 1, under suitable exclusion hypotheses on M, we establish an upper bound on the coefficients of the polynomial T_M(x,t) (resp., T_M(t,y)) in terms of girth g and the number of circuits of size g (resp., maximum cardinality h of hyperplanes and the number of hyperplanes of size h). The resulting characteristic polynomial bound extends the bound of Delaplane and Wu [Discrete Math. 312(12-13) (2012) 2062-2068] to simple U_{g-1,g+1}-free matroids satisfying n >= r + c_g, thereby giving a partial affirmative answer to the question of extending their upper bound beyond binary matroids.

title: Saturation numbers of $K_3 \vee P_k$
summary: A graph $G$ is said to be $H$-saturated if $G$ contains no copy of $H$, but $G+e$ contains a copy of $H$ for any edge $e$ of $\overline{G}$. The saturation number of $H$, denoted by $\mathrm{sat}(n, H)$, is the minimum number of edges among all $H$-saturated graphs of order $n$. In this paper, we investigate the saturation number of $K_3 \vee P_k$ for $k \ge 3$ and show that $\mathrm{sat}(n, K_3 \vee P_k) = 3n - 6 + \mathrm{sat}(n-3, P_k)$ holds for all $n \ge a_k + 3$ and $k \ge 3$, which verifies the conjecture [Discrete Appl. Math, 394(2026) 62-80] on $\mathrm{sat}(n, K_s \vee P_k)$ is true for the case $s=3$, where $a_k = k$ for $3 \le k \le 5$, $a_k = 3 \cdot 2^{t-1} - 2$ for $k = 2t \ge 6$, and $a_k = 2^{t+1} - 2$ for $k = 2t + 1 \ge 7$.

title: The Choice Number of Random Graphs
summary: In 1999, Alon, Krivelevich and Sudakov conjectured that the choice number and chromatic number of the random graph $G(n,p)$ are asymptotically equal whenever $np\to\infty$. We prove their conjecture, showing that, with high probability, $$ \operatorname{ch}(G(n,p))=(1+o(1))χ(G(n,p)) $$ whenever $np\to\infty$. This improves the bound $\operatorname{ch}(G(n,p))\le(2+o(1))χ(G(n,p))$ for $np\to\infty$ and $p\le0.9$ obtained by Krivelevich and Vu in 2001. Our proof distinguishes two cases according to the size of independent sets. When independent sets of growing size are available, we establish a sharper uniform independent-set estimate that eliminates the factor-two loss in the bound of Krivelevich and Vu. When independent sets have bounded size, we establish a deterministic result showing that, under a suitable uniform independent-set condition, a proper colouring with bounded colour-class sizes yields an asymptotically matching upper bound on the choice number.

title: Multiple harmonic star sums involving central binomial coefficients as weights
summary: We consider weighted analogues of multiple harmonic and multiple $t$-harmonic star sums, where the "star" indicates non-strict inequalities between the summation indices. In the special case where all exponents are 2, which is of particular interest also for ordinary multiple ($t$-)harmonic star sums, we obtain evaluations in terms of simple finite sums. The proofs are based on several combinatorial identities which are of interest in their own right.

title: Solid-Resolving Sets on Directed Graphs
summary: A set $S \subseteq V(G)$ is a solid-resolving set of an undirected graph $G$ if each vertex can be distinguished from any vertex subset by their distances from the set $S$. Solid-resolving sets are a generalization of resolving sets, which have been studied extensively in the literature. We extend this concept to oriented graphs and directed graphs. In this setting, we first define solid-resolving sets for digraphs and then consider vertices that must be included in any solid-resolving set. We also study the solid-metric dimension, which is the minimum cardinality of a solid-resolving set of a given digraph. We determine the possible values of the solid-metric dimension for several common graph classes, including tournaments, directed trees, oriented cycles, complete bipartite graphs, as well as for Cartesian products of oriented paths and cycles. We also show via some examples that there is no trivial relation between the solid-metric dimension of a digraph and the solid-metric dimension of its underlying undirected graph. Furthermore, we show that the solid-metric dimension can increase or decrease by an arbitrary $k$ when one vertex is removed. Similarly, removing a single arc can decrease the solid-metric dimension by an arbitrary $k$; however, it can increase by at most 1. The arbitrary changes in solid-metric dimension indicate that the solid-metric dimension is a global, rather than a local, property.
comment: 24 pages, 5 figures. This paper has been presented in part in IWOCA 2026

title: A Bang-Jensen-Gutin-Li type condition for pancyclicity in digraphs
summary: Bang-Jensen-Gutin-Li type conditions are degree conditions for the existence of hamiltonian cycles in digraphs, which impose degree restrictions on nonadjacent vertices which have a common in-neighbor or a common out-neighbor. They can be viewed as directed analogues of both Fan-type conditions and heavy subgraph conditions in undirected graphs, and they also generalized the classes of locally semicomplete digrahs, loclaly in-semicomplete digraphs, and locally out-semicomplete digraphs. In this paper, we prove what is, to our knowledge, the first Bang-Jensen-Gutin-Li type condition for pancyclicity in digraphs. More precisely, let $D$ be a strong digraph with order $n\ge 3$. We show that, if for every $u\in V(D)$ belonging to a dominated nonadjacent pair or a dominating nonadjacent pair, we have $d(u)\ge n$, then $D$ is pancyclic, unless $D$ belongs to one of two well-characterized classes of exceptional digraphs.

title: Two families of Young tableaux with periodic walls: Counting formulas and differential transcendence
summary: Banderier, Marchal, and Wallner studied the enumeration problem for Young tableaux with walls. These are similar to standard Young tableaux, except that local decreases are allowed at some walls. In 2021, Banderier and Wallner counted Young tableaux with periodic walls, in which the elementary blocks are Young diagrams of shape $(2,2)$. They obtained exact counting formulas for $30$ of the $32$ classes up to symmetry. In this paper, we first derive recurrences for counting the remaining two classes of Young tableaux with periodic walls. We then prove that their counting exponential generating functions are differentially transcendental. Consequently, they are neither D-algebraic nor D-finite. This disproves a conjecture of Banderier and Wallner.

title: Sharp Bounds for Graph-Codes Avoiding Complete Bipartite Differences
summary: Let $d_{K_{s,t}}(n)$ be the largest fraction of all graphs on $[n]$ in a family containing no two distinct members whose symmetric difference is a copy of $K_{s,t}$. We determine this maximum density for every fixed pair of positive integers $s,t$. If both part sizes are odd, it is known that the density is exactly $1/2$. Otherwise, let $2h$ be the largest even part size. We prove $$ d_{K_{s,t}}(n)=Θ_{s,t}(n^{-h}). $$ For $h>1$, this improves the general $O_{s,t}(1/n)$ upper bound obtained from Alon's two-copy gluing theorem~\cite{Alon2024}. The sharp bounds for even stars were already proved by Alon and are recovered as special cases. The upper bound uses the Frankl--Füredi forbidden-intersection theorem. For the lower bound, we construct binary linear codes using BCH codes. When exactly one part size is even, we assign to each edge the sum of the binary vectors assigned to its endpoints. When both part sizes are even, we identify these vectors with elements of a finite field and assign to each edge the product of its endpoint elements. In both cases, every copy of $K_{s,t}$ has a nonzero syndrome.

title: Optimal $K_t$-free list colorings and the Pollyanna property of graphs with no triangular wheel
summary: A wheel consists of an induced cycle of length at least four and a vertex with at least three neighbors on the cycle. Let $\cal T$ be the class of graphs with no wheel containing a triangle. We prove that, for every $G\in\cal T$ and every integer $t\ge3$, the $K_t$-free chromatic and choice numbers both equal $\lceil{ω(G)/(t-1)}\rceil$. We further prove that $\cal T$ is $k$-strongly linear-Pollyanna for every integer $k\ge2$, and hence is linear-Pollyanna. In particular, the class of wheel-free graphs is Pollyanna, answering Problem 10.2 of Chudnovsky, Cook, Davies and Oum.

title: Combinatorial decompositions of strict partitions and multi-sum Rogers-Ramanujan type identities
summary: While multi-sum Rogers-Ramanujan type identities have been extensively investigated through Bailey pairs, the constant term method, complex contour integration, and related techniques, many still lack an intrinsic combinatorial understanding. In this paper, we establish combinatorial interpretations for several families of triple-sum identities via structural decompositions of strict partitions. For one of these families, we extend the underlying combinatorial framework to obtain a general $(m+1)$-fold multi-sum identity. Leveraging these partition-theoretic interpretations, we construct explicit bijective proofs for all the corresponding identities. As an application, this constructive approach naturally yields some parameterized generalizations.

title: Regular Graphs Without Isomorphic Bisections
summary: A graph is bisectable if its vertex set can be split into two sets inducing isomorphic subgraphs. Ando conjectured that every cubic graph is bisectable, and Das, Pokrovskiy, and Sudakov proved it for large enough connected cubic graphs. We give a constructive proof that, for every $d\geq5$, there exists a non-bisectable $d$-regular graph of even order.

title: Scott-type inequalities for trinomial $h^*$-polynomials
summary: Motivated by Scott's inequality for lattice polygons, we study normalized volume bounds for lattice polytopes $\mathcal{P}$ with $h^*$-polynomials $1+at^k+bt^\ell$, where $a,b\ge1$ and $1\le k<\ell$. For $\ell>2k$, the coefficients satisfy $a+1\le b$, and consequently ${\rm vol}(\mathcal{P})\le2b$. In the complementary range $k<\ell\le2k$, we establish the dimension-independent bound \[ {\rm vol}(\mathcal{P})\le(2b+1)(k+\ell). \] On the boundary $\ell=2k$ with $b\ge2$, the sharper Scott-type inequality ${\rm vol}(\mathcal{P})\le4k(b+1)$ holds, confirming a conjecture of Higashitani, Nill, and the author. Equality holds if and only if $k=1$ and $a=3b+3$. Moreover, when $\ell=2k$ and $k,b\ge2$, we obtain an upper bound depending only on $b$.

title: Maximum length and size of simultaneous core partitions with distinct parts
summary: We give, for the first time, a formula for the largest size of an $(s,t)$-core partition with distinct parts valid for every coprime pair. We also determine the greatest number of parts of an $(s,t)$-core partition whose successive parts differ by at least $D$, whenever $\gcd(s,t)\le D$, removing the restrictions on the core parameters in the formula of Burson, Sisneros-Thiry, and Straub. The size formula uses a column description and a single Dedekind sum. The length formula uses coefficients from the Euclidean algorithm and satisfies a recurrence in smaller core parameters. We construct partitions attaining each maximum.

title: On Cayley Graphs of Skew Braces and Their Distances
summary: We introduce the left and right Cayley graphs of a finite skew brace $(A,\cdot, \circ)$ with a connection set $T\subset A$, as a directed multigraph with additive and multiplicative edges, depicting the operations $\cdot$ and $\circ$ respectively. We compute the distance from $a$ to $a\circ b$ in these Cayley graphs in terms of factorization lengths over $T$. As an application, we provide a characterization of the ideals of a skew brace in terms of their corresponding Cayley graphs.

title: A characterization of graphs attaining a lower bound on the dissociation number
summary: The dissociation number ${\rm diss}(G)$ of a graph $G$ is defined as the maximum cardinality of a vertex subset $D\subseteq V(G)$ such that the induced subgraph $G[D]$ has maximum degree at most $1$. In 2023, Bock, Pardey, Penso and Rautenbach [J. Graph Theory 103 (2023), 661--673] showed that ${\rm diss}(G)\ge n-\frac{1}{3}(m+k+c_1)$ where $n, m, k, c_1$ denote the numbers of vertices, edges, components and induced cycles of length $1$ modulo $3$ in $G$ and they also established a complete characterization of extremal graphs under the vertex-disjoint cycle constraint. Although this partial characterization offers very valuable structural insights, it excludes many simple extremal graphs. So they posed a natural question: How can all extremal graphs be comprehensively characterized without restrictions? In this paper, we give a recursive characterization of all graphs attaining equality in this bound.
comment: Dissociation sets; dissociation number; maximum; extremal graphs

title: The sparse regularity method for graphs with few even-cycle homomorphisms
summary: Let $C_k$ denote a cycle on $k$ vertices. Pascadi (2026) established a removal lemma for $C_{2k+1}$ in graphs with few $C_{2k}$-homomorphisms under a dense-pairs condition, using Schatten--von Neumann norms and entropy methods. We give a short proof of a version with more restrictive partition and diagonal requirements, extending the combinatorial approach of Conlon, Fox, Sudakov and Zhao (2021) without using Pascadi's Schatten-norm regularity framework. We illustrate the method with a known sparse removal statement for odd product equations in finite groups.

title: The Schur positivity of Lucas binomial differences
summary: For positive integers $a\le b\le c\le d$ with $ad=bc$, we prove that the Lucas binomial coefficients satisfy $(-1)^{a+1}(L_{b,c}[X]-L_{a,d}[X])\in\mathbb{N}[e_1[X],e_2[X],h_2[X]]$, resolving Bergeron's conjecture on Schur positivity in two variables. We also prove the same positivity for $L_{u,v}[X]-e_1[X]^{uv-rs}L_{r,s}[X]$ when $rs<uv$. Using Lucas atoms, we establish $e$-positivity for degree-adjusted Lucas multinomial differences under dominance order.

title: Counting transversals in Latin squares over groups of even order
summary: The number of transversals in a Latin square $L(G)$ whose rows and columns are indexed by a finite group $G$ has been determined computationally for all $G$ of order at most $23$ and for $C_{25}$. However, computation of the number of transversals of $L(G)$ has until now been considered intractable for all non-cyclic groups $G$ of order $32$. We show, for a group $G$ containing an order $2$ normal subgroup $N$, that the image of a transversal in $L(G)$ under the quotient mapping from $G$ to $G/N$ is a $2$-plex in $L(G/N)$. We then derive linear algebraic conditions that determine the number of transversals in $L(G)$ whose image under the quotient mapping is a given $2$-plex in $L(G/N)$. This allows us to count transversals in $L(G)$ by examining all $2$-plexes in $L(G/N)$. Although we can simplify the counting of $2$-plexes in $L(G/N)$ by taking advantage of their symmetry group, the linear algebraic conditions can vary over a symmetry class of $2$-plexes. However, in the case that $G$ takes the splitting form $C_2 \times H$, the linear algebraic conditions become invariant over each symmetry class and so the counting of transversals in $L(C_2 \times H)$ reduces to counting the $2$-plexes in $L(H)$ under the action of their symmetry group. We illustrate the power of these techniques by computing the exact number of transversals in $L(C_2^5)$.

title: Generalizing Praeger--Xu graphs
summary: We uniformly study directed Praeger--Xu graphs and Praeger's generalized family $\overrightarrow{\operatorname{PX}}(Γ,r,s)$, without requiring that $s\mid r$ and $Γ$ is an undirected graph. Assuming that $Γ\times\overrightarrow{K}_2$ is connected, we determine the full automorphism group of $\overrightarrow{\operatorname{PX}}(Γ,r,s)$ for every $r$ and $s$, prove connectivity, characterize vertex-transitivity, and give an equivalent criterion for $t$-arc-transitivity. We also study when $\overrightarrow{\operatorname{PX}}(Γ,r,s)$ is a Cayley graph. We also give two applications. First, we give a new family of twin-free connected arc-transitive digraphs of valency $4$ whose vertex stabilizers have exponential growth. We also give a connected regular digraph that is not vertex-transitive but whose direct product with a directed cycle is Cayley.

title: On the facets of the Cayley polytope of Stanley's triangulation
summary: Disjunctions over the cells of a triangulation arise in formulations of piecewise-linear functions. For a poset $P$ on $[d]$, we study the convex hull $D$ of the simplices of Stanley's triangulation of the order polytope of $P$, each lifted by its own indicator vector. Via the Cayley trick, for any disjunction of full-dimensional polytopes, the facets of the convex hull other than those described by the bounds on the indicator variables correspond to the facet normals of the Minkowski sum of the polytopes, and each is described by the full optimal big-M lifting of the supporting inequality with that normal of any one polytope. For Stanley's triangulation, with $M(P)$ the Minkowski sum of its simplices, lifting only the facet-describing inequalities of the simplices need not suffice, unlike some other cases; we show that it suffices if and only if $M(P)$ is alcoved, if and only if deleting one element of $P$ leaves a chain. Otherwise, the coefficients of the additional facet-describing inequalities are governed by the least number $\ell(P)$ of elements whose deletion leaves a chain: for fixed $\ell(P)$, the largest entry of a primitive facet normal grows like $d^{\ell(P)-1}$, and it can be exponential in $d$ if $\ell(P)$ grows with $d$. For $d \geq 3$ and $\ell(P)\leq2$ the sharp bound is $d-2$.

title: Facet normals of Minkowski sums of staircase simplices
summary: Staircase simplices are the simplices of the standard (Freudenthal--Kuhn) triangulation of $[0,1]^d$ and of Stanley's triangulations of order polytopes. We study the facet normals of their Minkowski sums and how the number of summands constrains the size of primitive integer normals. We characterize the normals attainable with a prescribed number of summands in terms of $d-1$ linearly independent zero-one vectors orthogonal to the normal, whose supports have an intersection graph that can be colored with one color per summand. This gives a combinatorial characterization of the least number of summands needed to realize a normal. For two summands, all primitive normals have entries in $\{-1,0,1\}$, and we determine which of them occur. For three summands we bound every entry in absolute value by $3^{(d-2)/3}$ and construct normals with entries of order $θ^d$, $θ$ the plastic number; for four summands a second construction gives entries of order $ψ^d$, $ψ$ the supergolden ratio. Since $ψ>3^{1/3}$, the largest coefficients for three and four summands are exponentially separated. For vectors with at most two distinct nonzero entry values, we determine the least number of summands exactly, using a matching-rank formula proved by exterior algebra and representations of symmetric groups. With no restriction on the number of summands, the maximum coefficient equals the classical maximum for facets of $0/1$-polytopes in the same dimension.

title: Degree-list Kempe equivalence for 3-connected graphs
summary: In a proper coloring, a Kempe change interchanges two colors on a connected component of the subgraph they induce. For a fixed list assignment $L$, a Kempe change is $L$-valid if it transforms an $L$-coloring into another $L$-coloring. We prove that if $G$ is a $3$-connected graph other than a complete graph or the triangular prism, and $L$ is a list assignment with $|L(v)|\ge d_G(v)$ for every vertex $v$, then $G$ has a proper $L$-coloring and any two such colorings can be transformed into one another by a finite sequence of $L$-valid Kempe changes. This proves a conjecture of Chakraborty, Feghali and Mahmoud.

title: Positivity for a $t$-analogue of refined Littlewood-Richardson rules
summary: In 2010, Haglund, Luoto, Mason and van Willigenburg proved that the product of a Schur function $s_λ$ and a Demazure atom $A_γ$ expands positively in terms of Demazure atoms, and interpreted the coefficients as the number of Littlewood-Richardson skew skyline tableaux of a given shape and a filling type. Extending this approach, they further established the positive expansion for the product of a Schur function $s_λ$ and a quasisymmetric Schur function $S_α$, or of a Schur function $s_λ$ and a Demazure character $κ_γ$. In particular, the latter provides a refinement of the classical Littlewood-Richardson rule. We present a natural $t$-analogue of these positive expansions by deriving the expansion for a product of a Hall-Littlewood polynomial $P_λ(t)$ and a $t$-Demazure atom $E_γ(t)$ in terms of $t$-Demazure atoms. The corresponding coefficients are $\mathbb{N}\,[t,1-t]$-positive; that is, they are polynomials with nonnegative integer coefficients in $t$ and $1-t$, and they are interpreted in terms of standard Young tableaux. We take the approach of connecting the multiplication coefficients with the LLT polynomials, which differs from the combinatorial insertion arguments of Haglund, Luoto, Mason and van Willigenburg.

title: From skew Combinatorial Nullstellensatz to sharp Ax-Katz congruences and zero counts
summary: We give a unified account of zero counting in finite-field polynomial rings with commuting variables twisted by a common automorphism. A decomposition into fixed-field slices connects skew evaluation with ordinary polynomial evaluation. First, we derive a slice coefficient formula from the skew Combinatorial Nullstellensatz and use it to deduce skew Chevalley-Warning, including the sufficient condition $n>h\sum_i d_i$. Next, classical Ax-Katz gives the corrected integer congruence $Q^{\max\{0,\lceil(n-h\sum_i d_i)/D\rceil\}}\mid N+(M-1)δ$. We construct homogeneous examples proving optimality for every positive degree table and every number of variables. We also establish a sharp lower bound with a prescribed zero, an input-sensitive coefficient-filtration refinement, and transfers of known bounds for nonlinear zero sets. Detailed calculations explain the origin correction, incomplete norm blocks, and the distinction between characteristic-$p$ summation and higher integer divisibility. Existing geometric, interpolation, and counting theorems are explicitly attributed.

title: Minimum Contagious Sets in Trees with Degree-Proportional Thresholds
summary: We investigate how large the minimum size of a contagious set can be among trees of a fixed order. Given a graph $G$ and $ρ\in[0,1]$, an inactive vertex $u$ becomes active when at least $\lceil{ρd_G(u)\rceil}$ of its neighbors are active. An initial set of active vertices is contagious if the process eventually activates every vertex. We obtain exact values for the minimum size of a contagious set in perfect $d$-ary trees. We then determine the exact maximum of this minimum size over all trees of order $n$. We establish this result by bounding the number of pairwise disjoint resistant sets, each of which must intersect every contagious set, and constructing trees that attain the resulting bounds. Finally, by bounding the change in the minimum size of a contagious set under a leaf exchange, we show that, for $0<ρ\leq1$ and $n\geq2$, every integer between $1$ and this maximum occurs as the minimum size of a contagious set in a tree of order $n$.

title: P-stable degree sequence regions for bipartite and directed graphs
summary: The switch Markov chain is a natural method for sampling graph realizations with a prescribed degree sequence, and $P$-stability is a general sufficient condition for its rapid mixing. Since $P$-stability is often difficult to verify directly, we develop an approach based on the simpler and more readily verifiable property of \emph{full graphicality}. We consider bidegree sequence regions obtained by fixing the two class sizes, the common degree sum, and lower and upper bounds for the degrees in each class. Such a region is fully graphic if every bidegree sequence satisfying these constraints has a bipartite realization. Our main result shows that every fully graphic region of this form is $P$-stable. More precisely, for class sizes $n$ and $m$, the perturbation ratio is at most $(nm)^5$. It follows from a known theory that the switch Markov chain is rapidly mixing on every such region. We also show that full graphicality can be tested on a canonical extremal bidegree sequence and use this characterization to derive several new explicit sufficient conditions. By encoding loopless directed graphs as bipartite graphs, we develop a parallel theory for directed degree sequences. This gives analogous extremal characterizations, sufficient conditions for full graphicality, and $P$-stability and rapid-mixing results for directed degree-sequence regions. The encoding process allows most corresponding statements for the two cases to be formulated and proved in one run.

title: The counts of parity-odd vs even late-growing permutations in the group $\mathbb{S}_{2p-1}$ differ by $(-1)^p$
summary: A permutation $σ\in\mathbb{S}_n$ of objects $\{1,\ldots,n\}$ is called \emph{late-growing} if its partial sums never exceed the respective partial sums of the `average' permutation (with the arithmetic mean $n^{-1}\cdot\sum_{i=1}^n i = (n+1)/2$ of $1,\ldots,n$ on average at each entry $σ(i)$): $\sum_{i=1}^k σ(i) \leqslant k\cdot (n+1)/2$ for all positive $k\leqslant n$. We prove that for $n=2p-1$ odd, the set $Φ_p\subseteq \mathbb{S}_{2p-1}$ of late-growing permutations is partitioned into parity-even vs odd elements, $Φ_p = Φ_p^{+} \sqcup Φ_p^{-}$, in an almost symmetric way: $| Φ_p^{+} | - | Φ_p^{-} | = (-1)^{p+1}$. The proof is constructive: by viewing the permutations $σ\inΦ_p$ as constrained walks on the integral lattice $\mathbb{Z}$, we describe two filters that pair all but one element in $Φ_p^{+}$ versus $Φ_p^{-}$; the remaining walk $σ^*$ with monotonically growing step amplitudes determines the dominant parity subset.
comment: Proof of the claim from arXiv:2605.11137 [math.CO]; sequel to arXiv:2610.08636 [math.NT]; 21 pages, 4 appendices, 6 tables, 6 figures

title: Properties C and D fail for $C_n^r$ whenever $n \equiv 2 \bmod 4, n\geq 6$ and $r\geq 4$
summary: Let $s(C_n^r)$ be the Erdős--Ginzburg--Ziv constant (zero-sums of length exactly $n$) and $η(C_n^r)$ the short zero-sum constant.
