Properties C and D of Gao et al.\ assert that every sequence of the extremal length without the relevant zero-sums has the form $T^{n-1}$. For even $n$ they imply $s(C_n^r)=2^r(n-1)+1$ and $η(C_n^r)=(2^r-1)(n-1)+1$. G.~Wang recently disproved both for $C_6^r$, $r\ge4$. We prove that both fail for $C_n^r$ for every $n\equiv2\pmod4$ with $n\ge6$ and every $r\ge4$. More precisely, for these $n$ we have: $s(C_n^r)\ge2^r(n-1)+2^{r-2}+1$.

title: A Sharp Distributional Lower Bound for Planar Discrepancy
summary: We prove that the unnormalized discrepancy function of every $n$-point set in the unit square has absolute value at least $c\sqrt{1+\log n}$ on a set of measure at least $η$, with absolute constants $c,η>0$. Consequently, its $L_p$-quasinorm is bounded below by $c\,η^{1/p} \sqrt{1+\log n}$ for every $p>0$.

title: On the unit group of some triquadratic fields
summary: In this paper, we calculate the unit groups and the $2$-class numbers of the fields $ \mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{2}, \sqrt{q}, \sqrt{rs})$, where $q\equiv3\pmod4$, $r$ and $s$ are distinct prime numbers satisfying some congruent conditions. As an application of our main results, we derive the precise 2-class number for each field in our family. Furthermore, we show that Greenberg's conjecture is verified for several infinite families of real biquadratic fields.

title: Two parametric $q$-supercongruences from Andrews' multi-series transformation
summary: Recently, Guo and Guo (Results Math $76:37, ~2021$) obtained curious $q$-analogues of the following two supercongruences conjectured by Guo and Schlosser \cite[Conjectures $12.6$ and $12.7$]{GuoSclssr ConstApprox 21}: \begin{align*} \sum_{n=0}^{(p-1)/3} (6n+1) \frac{\left(\frac{1}{3}\right)_n^{4}(2n)!} {(n!)^{4}\left(\frac{2}{3}\right)_{2n}} \equiv p \pmod{p^{3}} \qquad \text{for primes } p\equiv 1 \pmod{3}, \end{align*} \begin{align*} \sum_{n=0}^{(p+1)/3} (6n-1) \frac{\left(-\frac{1}{3}\right)_n^{4}(2n)!} {(n!)^{4}\left(-\frac{2}{3}\right)_{2n}} \equiv p \pmod{p^{3}} \qquad \text{for primes } p\equiv 2 \pmod{3}, \end{align*} where $(z)_n=z(z+1)\cdots(z+n-1)$ denotes the shifted factorial. In this paper, we establish a one-parameter extension of them. The main ingredients of our proofs are the creative microscoping method developed by Guo and Zudilin \cite{guo2019q} and Andrews' multi-series transformation.

title: On the evenness of coefficients of modular forms
summary: We study the density of primes such that $a_p$ is divisible by a prime above $2$ for modular forms $f = \sum_{n \ge 1} a_n q^n$ of small levels. First, we reduce the problem to low weight and odd level, or a mod $2$ CM type form. Then, we provide calculations for the evenness of particular newforms. In particular, we provide a list of levels where this "evenness" can be computed exactly for all the forms with trivial nebentypus.

title: A secondary term in the first moment of cubic $L$-functions over function fields
summary: Let $q$ be a fixed odd prime power with $q\equiv2\pmod3$. We study the first moment of primitive cubic Dirichlet $L$-functions over $\Fq(T)$, ordered by their genus. By averaging the rational sieve variable in the double Dirichlet series of Hong and Fang, we obtain meromorphic continuation beyond the secondary polar divisor. Combining this continuation with the cubic Gauss-sum residues computed by David, Florea and Lalín gives an explicit term of order $q^{5g/6}$, with a real coefficient depending on $g$ modulo $6$, and an error $O_{q,\eps}(q^{(23/28+\eps)g})$. The periodic coefficient is not identically zero. The proof uses an exact first difference supplied by the functional equation, an Euler product for the sieve average, and Bochner's tube theorem in the Dirichlet variables.

title: Local obstructions and certified computations for perfect powers in power sums
summary: Let $S_k(x)=1^k+\cdots+x^k$. We study perfect-power values of $S_k(x)$ by combining local valuations with finite congruence certificates. For an irregular Bernoulli pair $(p,r)$ with $e=v_p(B_r)\ge1$, we prove a valuation formula uniform for $k\equiv r+1\pmod{p^e(p-1)}$, subject to an explicit condition on $v_p(x(x+1))$. This gives explicit families of nonexistence results in which both $x$ and $k$ are unbounded. We also determine all solutions of $S_k(x)=y^n$ for $3\le x\le10^6$ with $x\equiv0,3\pmod4$, leaving $k$ and $n\ge2$ unrestricted and including squares. This extends Hajdu's fixed-$x$ classification in the same residue classes. A uniform restriction on the normalized odd part of $S_k(x)$ and finite certificates exclude every $k\ge6$; the remaining exponents are checked by exact integer arithmetic. The certificates admit independent verification. We further prove a limitation of congruence tests of bounded prime-power depth and solve the equation for every $x\equiv28\pmod{5\,110\,664}$.

title: Height growth of rational self-maps
summary: Let $K$ be a number field or a function field of a curve. Let $f$ be a dominant rational self-map of a normal projective variety $X$ of dimension $d$ over $K$, and let $h_H\geq1$ be an ample Weil height. Let $λ_1(f)$ denote the first dynamical degree of $f$. We show that there is a constant $C_{f,h_H}>0$ such that, for any $n\geq1$ and any point $P\in X(\overline{K})$ with well-defined forward orbit, $h_H(f^n(P))\leq C_{f,h_H}h_H(P)n^{2(d-1)}λ_1(f)^n$ if $λ_1(f)>1$, and $h_H(f^n(P))\leq C_{f,h_H}h_H(P)n^{2d}$ if $λ_1(f)=1$. Over number fields, the proof combines a new uniform upper bound for arithmetic degrees with a uniform comparison of point heights. Over function fields, it relies on the corresponding uniform upper bound for geometric degrees on a projective model.

title: Squarefree Values of Random Polynomials
summary: In this paper we consider the error term in the expected count of squarefree values of a polynomial when evaluated at integers \(n\le N\). We prove a power saving on average over polynomials of fixed degree and height at most \(H\). Our results improve previous estimates of Browning and Shparlinski in that the required range of \(H\) is independent of the degree, but depends on \(N\)

title: On Lehmer's Problem
summary: Let $m\geq 2$ be an integer, and let $d\geq 2$ be an even integer. We study monic, reciprocal, non-cyclotomic polynomials $$ P(x)=x^d+a_{d-1}x^{d-1}+\cdots+a_1x+1\in\mathbb{Z}[x]. $$ For a fixed residue class $r\in\{0,1,\ldots,m-1\}$, we prove that there exists an effectively computable constant $c_{r,m}>1$ such that the Mahler measure $$ M(P)\geq c_{r,m} $$ for every irreducible polynomial $Q$ whose inner coefficients satisfy $$ a_j\equiv r\pmod m \qquad (1\leq j\leq d-1). $$ Moreover, we explicitly compute the constant $c_{r,m}$ in terms of $r$ and $m$. For the residue classes $r=2$, $r=3$, and $r=m-1$, we obtain improved lower bounds for suitable ranges of the modulus~$m$. We also consider monic, reciprocal, irreducible, non-cyclotomic polynomials whose inner coefficients belong to two distinct residue classes modulo $m$. More precisely, if the inner coefficients with odd indices are congruent to $a\pmod m$ and those with even indices are congruent to $b\pmod m$, where $a\not\equiv b\pmod m$, then we prove the existence of a constant $c_{m,a,b}>1$ such that the Mahler measure $$ M(P)\geq c_{m,a,b}. $$ These results solve Lehmer's problem for several families of polynomials. We also construct infinitely many examples in every even degree $d\geq 2$ of monic, reciprocal, irreducible, non-cyclotomic polynomials over $\mathbb{Q}$, together with explicit information about their Mahler measures. Our proofs rely on Y. Bilu's equidistribution theorem and its effective version proved by C. D'Andrea \emph{et al.}, as well as on a method developed by P. Borwein \emph{et al.} While it is natural to consider Bilu's equidistribution results in conjunction with the Borwein {\it et al}. method to Lehmer's problem, we are not aware of any previous work in the literature that employs this particular approach.

title: Zassenhaus Filtration and Ihara Constants
summary: Let $X$ be a curve over $\mathbb{F}_q$. Denote by $N(X)$ and $g(X)$ the number of $\mathbb{F}_q$-rational points and the genus of $X$ respectively. The Ihara constant \begin{equation*} A(q)=\limsup_{g(X)\to\infty}\frac{N(X)}{g(X)} \end{equation*} measures the asymptotic abundance of rational points on curves over $\mathbb{F}_q$. In this paper, we study the Zassenhaus filtration of pro-$p$ groups arising from class field towers. By combining Golod--Shafarevich theorem, embedding problems and central class field theory, we establish a new criterion for the infinitude of class field towers. As an application, we obtain an improvement on the best known lower bounds of Ihara constant $A(2)$ and $A(3)$ which are explicitly given by \[ A(2)\geq 0.317779\cdots \text{ and } A(3)\geq 0.496074\cdots. \]

title: Joint Extension Field Point Counts for Superelliptic Curves
summary: Fix a finite field $\mathbf{F}_q$, an integer $m\ge2$ prime to $q$, and $2\leκ\le m$. For a uniformly chosen $κ$-power-free polynomial $F\in\mathbf{F}_q[x]$ of degree $D$, we determine the limiting joint distribution of the affine point counts of $y^m=F(x)$ over $\mathbf{F}_q,\ldots,\mathbf{F}_{q^n}$ as $D\to\infty$, with $q$ and $n$ fixed. The probability generating function is a finite Euler product with explicit local factors. Equivalently, the limiting vector is a sum of independent closed-point contributions, each of which may affect several extension degrees. We obtain the formula by specializing the equidistribution and motivic Euler product formalism of Bertucci-Howe. We then compute means, covariances, and moment expansions as $q$ varies in a fixed reduced residue class modulo $m$, after the degree limit has been taken. The one-field specialization recovers the power-free affine point-count distribution of Cheong-Wood-Zaman.

title: Exploring topological features of a complex network of prime factors and composite numbers
summary: Prime numbers are mathematical concepts of particular interest because of their relative rarity among integers, as well as the relative unpredictability of their occurrence and density along the integer sequence. They constitute the building blocks of all other composite numbers, giving rise to the interesting and important concept of prime factorization, a process guaranteed by the fundamental theorem of arithmetic. Among the several works that have been reported about prime numbers and their interrelationship with composite numbers, some have considered derived graphs and/or networks. In this paper, we derive some topological features of a bipartite complex network of prime factors and composite numbers. More specifically, we prove mathematically that the network's diameter is exactly five regardless of the number of nodes. In particular, we show that certain nontrivial sub-networks have minimal diameter equal to four, which is, again, independent of the number of nodes as long as the network is large enough. The last shows that this network is of small-world type. We also characterize exactly the number of boundary nodes in the network and present a couple of algorithms to identify the most important, relevant, influential, or central nodes of the network. Finally, we focus on the computation of the information dimensions on the basis of Shannon and Tsallis entropies of the studied complex network. The results show both decreasing as the number of nodes increases. Furthermore, both entropies indicate that box coverings at the diameters \(\varepsilon=[3,4]\), group nodes into roughly the same number of boxes, independent of the number of nodes in the network.

title: Explicit Coleman integration over finite extensions of $\mathbb{Q}_p$
summary: Coleman integration is an important computational ingredient of the Chabauty--Coleman method and its extensions. We extend the Balakrishnan--Tuitman algorithm to general smooth projective curves with good reduction over arbitrary finite extensions of $\mathbb{Q}_p$, allowing both ramification and nontrivial residue degree. Given a suitable plane model and integral bases, we provide explicit precision bounds and an accompanying Magma implementation. As an application, a single-prime computation at $p=19$ over the unramified quadratic extension $\mathbb{Q}_{19^2}/\mathbb{Q}_{19}$ recovers all $35$ affine sporadic quadratic divisors on $X(s3,ns5)$ over $\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt5)$. Completeness is proved in an appendix using symmetric Chabauty and a Mordell--Weil sieve.

title: Finite-sum Identities and Supercongruences for Cubes of Catalan Numbers
summary: Let $C_k=\binom{2k}{k}/(k+1)$ be the $k$-th Catalan number, and let $p$ be an odd prime. We establish exact finite-sum identities that, together with known binomial supercongruences and reductions of Sun, yield $\sum_{k=0}^{(p-1)/2}\frac{C_k^3}{16^k}\equiv2-24y^2-\frac{5p^2}{2y^2}\pmod{p^3}$ when $p=x^2+3y^2\equiv1\pmod3$, and $\sum_{k=0}^{(p-1)/2}\frac{C_k^3}{(-8)^k}\equiv-1-48y^2-\frac{33p^2}{16y^2}\pmod{p^3}$ when $p=x^2+4y^2\equiv1\pmod4$. We also evaluate the corresponding sum with denominator $16^k(k+1)^2$, and obtain two weighted Catalan supercongruences. The finite identities follow from the ratios of consecutive summands, symmetry of double sums, and telescoping. All endpoint terms are retained over the rational numbers before any modular reduction. In each bilinear identity, one endpoint denominator equals $p$; its cancellation produces the necessary term of order $p^2$. The precise arithmetic inputs are stated separately.

title: Cross numbers and the characterization of finite abelian groups by length sets
summary: The Characterization Problem asks whether a finite abelian group with Davenport constant at least four is determined, up to isomorphism, by its system of length sets. This is a central inverse problem in non-unique factorization theory: it asks whether the possible numbers of irreducible factors retain enough information to recover the underlying class group. For rings of integers of algebraic number fields, an affirmative answer means that the ideal class group can be recovered from these factorization lengths alone. We resolve this problem for all homocyclic groups $C_n^r$: if $G$ is a finite abelian group with $\mathsf D(G)\ge4$ and $\mathcal L(G)=\mathcal L(C_n^r)$, then $G\cong C_n^r$. The cross number of a sequence is the sum of the reciprocals of the orders of its terms. This weighted measure of sequence length links zero-sum theory with half-factoriality, and determining its maximal value for minimal zero-sum sequences is a longstanding extremal problem. We also obtain an exact formula for the maximal cross number of minimal zero-sum sequences over subsets whose minimum distance is divisible by the rank of the ambient group minus one. For $G\cong C_{n_1}\oplus\cdots\oplus C_{n_r}$ with $1<n_1\mid\cdots\mid n_r$ and $r\ge\max\{2,n_r-2\}$, we prove \[ \mathsf K(G,r-1)=1+(r-1)\sum_{p\mid n_1} \left(1-p^{-\mathsf v_p(n_1)}\right), \] which is a key ingredient in resolving the Characterization Problem for homocyclic groups.

title: Three Quadratic Recurrences Modulo 3: What We Can Prove and What We Can Guess
summary: We study three innocent-looking recurrences modulo $3$, each built from squares of two earlier terms. One of them turns out to be secretly $\textit{linear}$, and we can compute its periods exactly. One is a $\textit{permutation}$ hiding a small, perfectly orderly piece inside a large, random-looking one. The third looks thoroughly random, but it still has a few provable features. Along the way we meet open problems that need nothing beyond a first course in abstract algebra to state. This paper is a starting point, not the final word in any sense.

title: On real biquadratic number fields for which the $2$-Iwasawa module has rank $3$
summary: We investigate the stability of the $2$-rank in the cyclotomic $\mathbb{Z}_2$-extension of real biquadratic number fields. We determine several families of real biquadratic fields $F$ for which the ranks of the $2$-class group $A(F)$ and the associated $2$-Iwasawa module $A_\infty(F)$ are both equal to $3$. More precisely, we provide a complete classification of all fields $F=\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{q},\sqrt{d}),$ where $q\equiv 3\pmod{4}$ is a prime number and $d$ is an odd positive square-free integer, and all fields $F=\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{2q},\sqrt{d}),$ where $q\equiv 3\pmod{4}$ is a prime number and $d\equiv 1\pmod{4}$ is a positive square-free integer, for which $ \operatorname{rank}(A(F))=\operatorname{rank}(A_\infty(F))=3.$

title: A symmetric extension of Zhao's series for $ζ(5)$
summary: We prove a four-parameter extension of Zhao's series for $ζ(5)$. Restricting a Wilf-Zeilberger seed of Au to a hyperplane, we obtain a summand in five parameters with zero sum that is symmetric under all their permutations. Summing it from two different starting points gives two trigonometric closed forms, which we prove by Guillera's periodicity argument. The proof is self-contained, and also gives a companion series for $1/π^2$, which we have not found in the literature. Specializing the parameters at roots of unity, we obtain Borwein-Bradley-type identities whose products depend only on $x^2$, $x^3$, $x^4$ or $x^5$. Their Taylor coefficients are Apéry-like series for odd zeta values and for products of zeta values. In particular, we prove five identities conjectured by Au.

title: Frangible prime gaps
summary: A prime gap $(p_n, p_{n+1})$ is \textit{frangible} if the smallest prime divisor of every integer $m$ with $p_n<m<p_{n+1}$ is strictly less than the size of the gap, $p_{n+1}-p_n$. Gafni and Tao recently proved that the number of frangible gaps up to $X$ is $\ll X/\log^2 X$, answering a question of Erdős. They also showed that under the Dickson--Hardy--Littlewood prime tuples conjecture this number is $\sim c X/\log^2 X$ for a constant $c$, for which they obtained a rough estimate. We describe improved methods for estimating this constant under the same hypothesis, and establish that its value lies in $[2.7416, 2.7984]$, confirming a speculation of Gafni and Tao. In addition, we present the results of a complete survey of frangible gaps up to $10^{17}$. An ensuing empirical measurement of $c$ matches our estimate very well.

title: Results for distinct covering systems with a prime minimum modulus $q \ge 11$
summary: We prove that if the smallest modulus of a covering system is a prime $q \ge 11$, then the sum of the reciprocals of the moduli is at least $1+10^{-28}$. This improves on a previous more general bound of the first two authors in this particular case. We also show that it is impossible to construct a covering system using distinct multiples of $q$ as moduli. Finally, we show as a corollary that it is impossible to construct $10$ distinct covering systems with the property that no modulus is used in more than one of the covering systems.

title: Admissible sets of integers in imaginary quadratic fields of class number 1
summary: Let $\mathcal O_K$ be the ring of integers of a number field $K$. A finite subset $\mathcal H=\{η_1,\ldots,η_k\}\subset\mathcal O_K$ is said to be \emph{admissible} if for every prime ideal $\mathfrak p$ in $\mathcal O_K$, the reductions of the $η_i$ modulo $\mathfrak p$ do not represent every residue class. The diameter of a finite subset $S$ of $\mathcal O_K$ is defined to be \[\mathrm{diam}(S):= \max_{η_i,η_j\in S:η_i\neqη_j}|\mathcal N(η_i-η_j)|\] where $\mathcal N$ denotes the norm down to the rational field. This paper computationally investigates admissible subsets of rings of integers in imaginary quadratic fields of class number 1 (such as the Gaussian integers or the Eisenstein integers) that are large relative to their diameter. The motivation is twofold. Firstly, there is the improvement of results analogous to the question of an upper bound for the least gap between large rational primes, which has been one of the great number theoretic successes of the twenty-first century. A second motivation is that there is the opportunity to disprove a variation of the second Hardy-Littlewood conjecture. The calculations in the paper provide new records on the smallest distance between primes in the fields in question, and explicit counter-examples to a generalisation of the second Hardy-Littlewood conjecture in all bar one of the fields.

title: Finiteness theorems for trace Euclidean quadratic lattices over totally real number fields
summary: Motivated by Clark's work on Euclidean quadratic forms, we introduce trace Euclidean and house Euclidean quadratic lattices over totally real number fields, and relate these concepts through the $p$-norm Euclidean property. We prove that, as $F$ varies over all totally real number fields of arbitrary degree, there are only finitely many positive definite trace Euclidean $\mathcal{O}_{F}$-lattices of arbitrary rank $n\ge1$, up to isometry. For every $p\in[1,\infty]$, the same finiteness holds for positive definite $p$-norm Euclidean lattices. We also classify all positive definite trace Euclidean lattices of rank one over real quadratic fields: there are exactly six isometry classes, and every such lattice is free. As a corollary, the trace Euclidean real quadratic fields are precisely $\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{2})$, $\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{5})$, and $\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{13})$.

title: Geometric progressions in distance sets in odd dimensions over prime fields
summary: For $E\subset\mathbb{F}_p^d$, let $Δ(E)=\{Q_d(x-y):x,y\in E\}$, where $Q_d(z)=z_1^2+\cdots+z_d^2$. We introduce and study the problem of the existence of nondegenerate three-term geometric progressions in the distance set $Δ(E)$ when $d$ is odd. If $M_{GP,d}(p)$ denotes the largest size of a set whose distance set contains no such progression, then, for every prime $p\geq7$ and every integer $m\geq0$, \[ p^mM_{GP,1}(p)\leq M_{GP,2m+1}(p) \leq4p^mM_{GP,1}(p). \] For all sufficiently large primes $p$, we also prove \[ p^{m+\frac{7}{26}}\leq M_{GP,2m+1}(p) \leq Cp^{m+\frac{16}{25}}, \] where $C$ is an absolute positive constant.

title: The Family $X_{qp^s}$ for Distinct Primes $q,p$ in Connection with Carmichael's Totient Conjecture
summary:
Shannon, Shiue, Saito and the author \cite{SSHS2025} studied the sets $X_k=\{n\in\mathbb{N}:\varphi(n)=k\}$ in connection with Carmichael's totient conjecture, and proved that for an odd prime $p
eq3$ and $s\in\{1,2,3,4\}$, $X_{2p^s}$ is empty whenever $2p^s+1$ is not prime (with $s=1$ fully characterized in both directions), conjecturing that this persists for every $s\ge1$. We resolve that conjecture in full, obtaining a complete characterization of $X_{2p^s}$ for every $s\ge1$ and every odd prime $p
eq3$, together with a parity dichotomy: $X_{2p^s}=\varnothing$ unconditionally whenever $s$ is even, while for odd $s$ both outcomes genuinely occur, determined exactly by the primality of $2p^s+1$. We then close the one remaining gap at $p=3$, where the proof technique degenerates, with a separate, unconditional characterization of $X_{2\cdot3^s}$. Building on these results, we consider the natural generalization $X_{qp^s}$, where $q
eq p$ are distinct primes and $s\ge1$. We show that this generalization splits into three cases of very different character. If $q$ and $p$ are both odd, the problem is trivial: $qp^s$ is odd, so $X_{qp^s}=\varnothing$ by elementary parity, with no case-analysis needed. If $q=2$, the problem is exactly the family $X_{2p^s}$ resolved above. If $p=2$, giving the ``mirror'' family $X_{2^sq}$ for an odd prime $q$, the problem is genuinely different. Beyond $s=1$, we give a complete resolution for $s=2$, recovering, with an explicit proof and solution sets, the qualitative dichotomy of \cite[Thm.~2.3.1]{SSHS2025}, but the problem remains open for $s\ge3$.

title: Hartl's dictionary and a transcendence characterization of equicharacteristic local shtukas with complex multiplication
summary: We update Hartl's dictionary between $p$-adic Hodge theory and its equicharacteristic analog to include aspects related to the Hodge--Tate filtration in $p$-adic Hodge theory and its equicharacteristic analog, the Hodge--Tate--Taguchi filtration. Using this update, we establish a transcendence characterization of equicharacteristic local shtukas with abelian Tannakian structure group, matching a result of Howe--Klevdal in the $p$-adic setting. A special case of this result says that a formal Drinfeld module over an equicharacteristic local field has complex multiplication if and only if the Hodge--Tate--Taguchi filtration on its $z$-adic Tate module is algebraic.

title: Dynamical Chowla conjecture for polynomials of several variables
summary: In 1965, Chowla conjectured that the mean value of the Liouville function at non-square one-variable polynomials is zero. This conjecture is a generalization of the prime number theorem (PNT). In 2022, Bergelson and Richter established a dynamical generalization of this form of the PNT. For non-square multivariate polynomials, one also expects that Chowla's conjecture is true. In this article, we extend Bergelson and Richter's result to multivariate polynomials whose Birch rank is sufficiently large in terms of their degree. We also establish analogous results for averages over integer points on algebraic varieties.

title: Counting Integral Matrices with Given Cubic Characteristic Polynomial
summary: We show that the number of $3\times 3$ matrices with given characteristic polynomial and entries in $\mathbb{Z}\cap [-H,H]$ is at most $c H^{3}(\log H)^{6}$ for all $H\ge 2$, where $c>0$ is an absolute constant.

title: Non-liftability of the field of norms of the $p$-adic false Tate curve extension
summary: Let $p\geq3$ be a prime number. We prove that the action of the Galois group on the field of norms of the $p$-adic false Tate curve extension $\mathbf{Q}_p\left(ζ_{p^\infty},p^{1/p^\infty}\right)$ of $\mathbf{Q}_p$ is not liftable to its Cohen ring with respect to any admissible coefficient field.

title: On almost perfect additive complements
summary: Let $A, B$ be infinite sets of non-negative integers with $n\in A+B$ for all sufficiently large integers $n$. We prove that if $A(x)B(x)-x$ does not tend to infinity, then $$\limsup_{x\to\infty}\frac{A(x)B(x)}{x}\in\Big[\frac{3}{2}, 2\Big].$$ The lower bound is sharp, and confirms a conjecture of Chen. Our proof is based on the weak limits and the convolution factorization theorem of Gabardo and Lai. A discrete proof of the same bound was also given by Zhang. Motivated by the known spectrum of perfect additive complements, we conjecture that the interval $(3/2, 8/5)$ is also excluded for almost perfect additive complements.

title: Galois groups of polynomials over a fixed number field: determinant methods in general boxes, resolvents, and quantitative counting
summary: Let $K$ be a fixed number field of degree $d$. We prove two determinant-method results for integral points over $\mathcal O_K$ in boxes whose coordinates may have different size bounds: a Bombieri-Pila type estimate for affine plane curves that retains the two separate coordinate bounds, and a Salberger-Browning covering theorem for affine surfaces. If $F\in\mathcal O_K[X_1,X_2]$ is irreducible and $T=\max B_1^{e_1}B_2^{e_2}$ over the monomials occurring in $F$, then \[ N_K(F;B_1,B_2)\ll T^\varepsilon \exp\!\left(d\frac{\log B_1\log B_2}{\log T}\right). \] For an absolutely irreducible surface in three variables we obtain a covering by $O(T^\varepsilon V_{3,K})$ bounded-degree auxiliary hypersurfaces, outside $O(T^\varepsilon V_{3,K}^2)$ exceptional integral points, where \[ V_{3,K}=\exp\!\left(d \left(\frac{\log B_1\log B_2\log B_3}{\log T}\right)^{1/2}\right). \] These are the number-field analogues of determinant-method estimates for unequal coordinate ranges developed in the rational setting by Browning and Heath-Brown, Salberger, Browning, and Chow-Dietmann. We then apply them to Galois resolvents of monic degree-$n$ polynomials over $K$. Independently, a large-sieve argument, in the tradition of Gallagher's probabilistic Galois theory, gives $O_{K,n}(N^{dn-d/2}\log N)$ exceptional separable polynomials, while effective Hilbert irreducibility over global fields gives subgroup-sensitive bounds with exponent $d(n-1+1/[S_n:G])$, up to logarithms. We record the interaction with the discriminant-square equation for even groups, congruence restrictions, and rectangular coefficient boxes. All determinant estimates used in the applications are proved in the paper; no conjectural global-field determinant statement is assumed.

title: Weighted density bounds for covering systems over Dedekind domains
summary: We study the density of uncovered sets arising from finite families of residue classes over Dedekind domains with finite residue norms. Building on the distortion method of Balister, Bollobás, Morris, Sahasrabudhe and Tiba, we prove a general weighted density criterion in which the weight attached to a prime ideal is allowed to vary. In the critical Mertens regime this yields, for every \(\varepsilon>0\), the admissible prime-ideal weight \[ 1+\frac{(\log N\mathfrak p)^3(\log\log N\mathfrak p)^{1+\varepsilon}}{N\mathfrak p}, \] up to a harmless modification at finitely many small prime ideals. This is asymptotically smaller than the fixed weight \(1+(\log N\mathfrak p)^{3+\varepsilon}/N\mathfrak p\) appearing in the earlier density theorem. The result is valid for systems of any fixed multiplicity and, for multiplicity one, requires the ideal moduli themselves to be distinct but not their norms. We then place the analytic hypotheses in Knopfmacher's Axiom~A framework. In the critical case of Axiom~A with exponent \(1\), the prime-ideal estimates needed by the weighted theorem are automatic. More generally, under Axiom~A with exponent \(ρ>0\), we prove a weighted mean-value theorem on ideals; in the subcritical range \(0<ρ<1\), a first-moment argument shows that sufficiently large moduli cover an arbitrarily small proportion of the ambient space. We also explain that the distortion construction itself only uses a compatible system of finite residue spaces with uniform fibres and a Chinese-remainder-type product structure, suggesting a possible extension beyond Dedekind domains. Finally, we show that a direct passage from the second moment to higher integer moments does not lower the logarithmic exponent \(3\) within this moment hierarchy.

title: Bounds on the number of squares in recurrence sequences: $y_{0}=b^{2}$ (II)
summary: For binary recurrence sequences, $\left( y_{k} \right)_{k \in \bbZ}$, arising from the solutions of generalised Pell equations, $X^{2}-dY^{2}=c$, where $y_{0}$ is any positive square and $c=-2^{\ell}p^{m}$ for an odd prime $p$ and non-negative integers $\ell$ and $m$, we show that there are at most $4$ distinct squares with $y_{k}$ sufficiently large. From this result, we also show that there are at most $7$ distinct squares when $y_{0}=1,2^{2},\ldots,7^{2}$, or once $d$ exceeds an explicit lower bound, without any conditions on the size of such squares.
journal_ref: Research in Number Theory, volume 12, article 6 (2026)

title: Congruences modulo powers of $7$ for partitions with colored odd parts
summary: Let $a_k(n)$ denote the number of partitions of $n$ in which even parts occur in one color and odd parts may occur in $k$ colors. We prove infinite families of congruences modulo powers of $7$ for $a_k(n)$ when $k \in \{4,5,7\}$. For each positive integer $α$, let $λ_{k,α}$ be the least nonnegative solution of $24λ_{k,α}\equiv-(k-2)\pmod{7^α}$. Then, we show that \[ a_k(7^αn+λ_{k,α}) \equiv 0\pmod{7^{\lfloor(α+1)/2\rfloor}} \] for every nonnegative integer $n$. These results extend congruences modulo $7$ of Hirschhorn and Sellers (2026) and complement Chen's (2025) congruences for the reciprocal crank parity function $a_3(n)$.

title: Spectral zeta functions in positive characteristic
summary: Spectral zeta functions and zeta-regularized determinants encode the spectrum of an operator in analytic functions. Over the completion $\mathbb C_\infty$ of an algebraic closure of $\mathbb F_q((π))$, two features of characteristic $p$ break this classical picture. Complex powers have exponents that vary only continuously in $\mathbb Z_p$, not analytically. Scalar traces record eigenvalue multiplicities only modulo $p$. We develop a resolvent-based theory that treats these two obstructions separately. For the first, inverse Stieltjes duality turns suitable scalar resolvents into locally analytic spectral distributions on $\mathbb F_q[[π]]$. A single exponent of the Mellin transform already determines the distribution and the entire Mellin family. We characterize exactly which power series arise in this way, by a growth condition on Carlitz moments. The criterion depends on the support: bounded Taylor coefficients are not sufficient. For stationary digit measures, the transform is the unique fixed point of an explicit contraction. The first $q-1$ nonconstant moments recover the measure. For the second, we replace traces by the Frobenius defect $F/σ(F)$, where $σ$ raises coefficients to their $q$th powers. On power series with small coefficients, this map is a group automorphism that preserves Gauss distances, and a convergent infinite product inverts it. Polynomial defects produce entire functions. They characterize exactly the diagonal spectra that are finite unions of forward Frobenius orbits, counted with multiplicity. For the shifted Carlitz operator, the resulting Fredholm determinant is a normalized reciprocal of the Anderson--Thakur function, and its Newton polygon is determined exactly.

title: On Hecke algebras at exceptional Eisenstein primes
summary: We study the structure over $\mathbb{Z}_p$ of the Hecke algebra acting on ordinary cusp forms in the Eisenstein, non-$p$-distinguished case. Our results and methods draw on four complementary approaches: deformation theory, through $R=\mathbf{T}$ theorems; Iwasawa theory, through connections to Sharifi's conjecture; $p$-adic $L$-functions, through an exceptional zero formula; and computational experiments using Magma. We also obtain new results regarding the Coleman--Greenberg conjecture.

title: On the Hasse principle for a block-diagonal form and a form of lower degree
summary: We investigate the Hasse principle for systems consisting of one form of degree $k$ which decomposes as a sum of $n$-ary forms, and one general form of degree $d < k$. By exploiting the block structure of the first form before applying Weyl differencing, we refine the method of Brandes and Parsell (arXiv:2003.04350) in this setting; in particular, for a sum of binary quartic forms and a quadratic form, the requirement $s > 516$ is relaxed to $s > 96$, which also improves on the bound $s > 100$ available for general forms.

title: On explicit formulas for Grassmannian polylogarithms and Gelfand-MacPherson forms
summary: We answer a question of Goncharov by showing that his Grassmannian $n$-logarithm can be recovered by integrating the Borel invariant form on the symmetric space $\mathrm{SL}_{n}(\mathbf{C})/\mathrm{SU}(n)$ over a naturally defined ideal simplex. As corollaries, we recover the finiteness of primitive canonical integrals of Brown and the evaluation for wheel graphs of Brown and Schnetz. We also compute explicitly the Gelfand-MacPherson forms for powers of the first Pontryagin class and give a general integral formula for the Gelfand-MacPherson forms associated to each component of the Pontryagin character.

title: Improved lattice-packing bounds in small dimensions
summary: We strengthen the upper bound on the density of a lattice packing in small dimensions. A lattice cannot have too many short vectors; we modify the Cohn--Elkies linear program accordingly by allowing the auxiliary function to be positive on a short interval beyond the minimum distance. For $11 \leq n \leq 16$, our bound is tighter than the three-point bound of Cohn, de Laat and Salmon. For $n \in [17, 23] \cup [25, 40] \cup [43, 57] \cup [62, 75]\cup [83, 91]$, our bound lies below the published numerical values of the Cohn--Elkies bound.

title: Absorption probabilities of random walks without symmetry or general position
summary: Let $S_1,S_2,\dots$ be a random walk in $\mathbb R^d$ with independent identically distributed increments. We show that, for every distribution of the increments and for every $n\ge1$, \[ \mathbb P\bigl[0\notin\mathrm{conv}(S_1,\dots,S_n)\bigr] = \sum_{m=1}^n\frac1{m!}\sum_{\substack{k_1,\dots,k_m\ge1\\ k_1+\dots+k_m=n}}\frac{1}{k_1\cdots k_m}\,\mathbb P\bigl[0\notin\mathrm{conv}(S^{(1)}_{k_1},\dots,S^{(m)}_{k_m})\bigr], \] where $S^{(1)},S^{(2)},\dots$ are independent copies of the walk. No symmetry, general position or moment assumptions are needed. The result rests on a deterministic identity: for arbitrary vectors $x_1,\dots,x_n$, the number of orderings for which the convex hull of the partial sums avoids the origin equals the number of permutations for which the convex hull of the cycle sums avoids it. We derive it from a permutation-averaging identity for valuations obtained in our earlier work. Consequences include the identities of Sparre Andersen and Spitzer, the distribution-free absorption probabilities of Kabluchko, Vysotsky and Zaporozhets, their generating function found by Petrov, Randon-Furling and Zaporozhets, and a formula for the probability that the origin is never absorbed.

title: An upper bound on the smallest singular value of dense signed random combinatorial matrices
summary: Let $M_n$ be an $n\times n$ random matrix with entries in $\{-1, 0, 1\}$, where each row is independently and uniformly sampled from the set of all vectors in $\{-1, 0, 1\}^n$ containing exactly $d$ nonzero entries, with $d=pn$ for some fixed constant $p\in(0,1/2]$. A recent result by one of the authors gives a lower bound of order $n^{-1/2}$ for the smallest singular value $s_n(M_n)$ of this model with high probability. In this paper, we establish a matching upper bound for $s_n(M_n)$. Specifically, there exists a constant $C_p>0$ depending only on $p$ such that \[ \forall \varepsilon >0 \qquad \mathbb{P} \left( s_n(M_n) \le \frac{\sqrt{d}}{\varepsilon^2 n} \right) \ge 1-C_p\left(\varepsilon + \frac{1}{\sqrt{d}}\right). \] Consequently, in the dense regime, the smallest singular value $s_n(M_n)$ of signed random combinatorial matrices is typically of order $n^{-1/2}$.

title: Efficiency--Complexity Tradeoff and Constrained Percolation
summary: We study the efficiency--complexity tradeoff for resource-limited agents through directed first-passage percolation. Nonnegative i.i.d. edge weights represent physical energy expenditure, while the logarithmic size of a constrained path family measures representational complexity. For translation-invariant families, a path-joining property yields deterministic large-distance costs in rational directions and joint convexity in constraint parameter and direction, under suitable moment and feasibility assumptions. Our main result concerns the limiting cost parameterized by path-family entropy. Using techniques from analytic combinatorics in several variables (ACSV), we establish its almost-sure existence and joint continuity in entropy and direction for nested families satisfying additional generating-function conditions, on the corresponding entropy range. Path-count asymptotics supply the change of parameter linking this cost to the constraint-parameterized cost. Two planar examples constrain the number of turns or the number of East-runs of length at least two.

title: Stationary Measures and Boundary Correlations for Multispecies Half-Line ASEP
summary: We construct stationary measures of the multispecies ASEP on the positive half-line, with injection of highest-priority particles at the left boundary, using vertex models. Our results extend existing constructions of Martin and Aggarwal-Nicoletti-Petrov for the full-line ASEP to the half-line. For the two-species process, we compute the joint distribution of occupation colors at the first two sites. We also partially address the connection with the half-space ASEP speed process.

title: Cutoff for random walks on nilpotent groups
summary: We study continuous-time random walks on finite nilpotent groups, allowing non-symmetric and nonuniform increment measures. Under a simple degree condition, sharp up to an absolute constant factor, we prove that total variation cutoff occurs if and only if the relaxation time is of smaller order than the mixing time. We establish a quantitative reduction to the Abelianization that preserves relaxation times and compares mixing profiles. Combining this reduction with a Gaussian approximation and the third-named author's cutoff criterion for diffusions yields the cutoff characterization.

title: Extensions of a family of Linear Cycle Sets whose underlying group is a product of two cyclic groups
summary: We use the linear cycle set cohomology in order to compute extensions of a non trivial linear cycle sets whose underlying additive group is a product of two cyclic groups.

title: A crystallographic quotient of the framed braid group and associated flat manifolds
authors: Paulo Cesar Cerqueira dos Santos Júnior
summary: We study the quotient of the framed braid group $FB_n$ by the commutator subgroup of the framed pure braid group $FP_n$. We prove that $$ \frac{FB_n}{[FP_n,FP_n]}\cong\mathbb Z^n\rtimes\frac{B_n}{[P_n,P_n]}, $$ and, for $n\geq3$, that this quotient is a crystallographic group of dimension $n(n+1)/2$ with holonomy group $S_n$. We investigate its finite-order elements and conjugacy classes, prove that it has no elements of finite even order, and construct Bieberbach subgroups with prescribed finite $2$-group holonomy. Starting from suitable Bieberbach subgroups of $\frac{B_n}{[P_n,P_n]}$, we then construct Bieberbach subgroups of the framed quotient whose associated compact flat manifolds are torus bundles over the corresponding unframed flat manifolds. We describe these bundles through the generalized Calabi construction and determine their orientability, first Betti numbers, and the centers of their fundamental groups. As an application, we study a family with cyclic holonomy of odd order, obtaining a criterion for the existence of flat Kähler structures, and indicate how the same construction applies to cyclic holonomy of $2$-power order.

title: Absolutely universal projective embeddings of long-root geometries of orthogonal type
summary: Let $G$ be a split Chevalley group of type $B_n$ ($n \geq 3$) or $D_n$ ($n \geq 4$), let $L$ be its Lie algebra and $Γ$ its long-root geometry, namely $Γ$ is the line-grassmannian of the polar space associated to $G$. It is well known that $L$ hosts a projective embedding of $Γ$, called the adjoint embedding, which realizes $Γ$ as a projective variety in the projective geometry of the underlying vector space of $L$. It is also known that $Γ$ admits the absolutely universal projective embedding, which is such that all projective embeddings of $Γ$ can be obtained from it as projections. When the field $F$ over which $G$ is defined is finite, the universal embedding of $Γ$ is just the same as the adjoint embedding. The same is not necessarily true when $F$ is infinite. Indeed, as we shall prove in this paper, the universal projective embedding of $Γ$ lives in a direct sum $K\oplus L$ for an $F$-vector space $K$, the dual of which is isomorphic to the derivation space $\mathrm{Der}(F)$ of $F$, which in general is non-trivial. Accordingly, the adjoint embedding of $Γ$ is universal if and only if $\mathrm{Der}(F)$ is trivial, namely $F$ is either perfect of positive characteristic or algebraic over its minimum subfield.

title: Counterexamples to congruences in finite p-groups
summary: Let $K$ be a conjugacy class of a finite $p$-group $G$. Héthelyi, Külshammer and the author asked whether the number of conjugacy classes contained in $KK^{-1}$ is always congruent to $1$ modulo $p-1$, and whether, dually, the number of irreducible constituents of $χ\overlineχ$ is congruent to $1$ modulo $p-1$ for every $χ\in\mathrm{Irr}(G)$. We construct a group of order $7^7$ for which both congruences fail.

title: On the isomorphism problem of Cayley digraphs
summary: A finite group $G$ is called a DCI-group provided any two Cayley digraphs $Cay(G,S)$ and $Cay(G,T)$ are isomorphic iff the two connection sets $S$ and $T$ are images of each other via automorphisms of the group $G$. Building on the vast literature on CI- and DCI-groups we present an updated list of possible DCI-groups. In addition, we give an alternative proof that does not rely on deep results from group theory. We also point out the three most important open problems related to the classification of DCI-groups.

title: On 2-Arc-Transitive Cayley Graphs of Nonabelian Characteristically Simple Groups
summary: The classification of symmetric Cayley graphs has attracted considerable attention. Results have been obtained for finite abelian groups and nonabelian simple groups. However, the problem remains open for finite nonabelian characteristically simple groups, although some results on normality for small valencies are known. In this paper, we determine the possible structures of automorphism groups $X$ of connected 2-arc-transitive Cayley graphs $Γ$ of $G\cong T^k$, where $T$ is a finite nonabelian simple group and $k\geqslant2$. In the quasiprimitive case, we prove that $G\unlhd X$, $Γ$ is complete, or $X$ is of product action type with restricted parameters. For the non-quasiprimitive case, we determine the possible structures of the quasiprimitive normal quotients of $Γ$.

title: Word Trace Formulas over Compact Groups and Connected Cumulants
summary: We compute the expected value of the product of traces for a finite set of words within any compact subgroup of $\mathcal(N)$. Furthermore, we establish a sufficient condition under which these values determine that the product of the conjugacy classes of the words contains the identity.

title: The measure equivalence classification of Baumslag-Solitar groups
summary:
In this article we show that all the nonamenable Baumslag-Solitar groups with nonunimodular Bass-Serre tree, i.e., $\mathrm{BS}(p,q)$ with $|p|,|q| 
eq 1$ and $|p|
eq |q|$, are measure equivalent to each other, thereby completing the measure equivalence classification of Baumslag-Solitar groups: each $\mathrm{BS}(p,q)$ belongs to one of three measure equivalence classes according to whether it is amenable ($|p|=1$ or $|q|=1$), virtually isomorphic to $\mathbf{F}_n 	imes \mathbf{Z}$ ($|p|=|q|
eq 1$), or is nonamenable with nonunimodular Bass-Serre tree ($|p|,|q| 
eq 1$ and $|p| 
eq |q|$). More generally, we obtain the similar classification of the generalized Baumslag-Solitar groups of rank $1$ (i.e., groups that act cocompactly on a tree with edge and vertex stabilizers infinite cyclic). Our proof also establishes a classification of all treeable lcsc groups into exactly six measure equivalence classes. Our new contribution which completes this taxonomy is: all nonunimodular nonamenable treeable lcsc groups are measure equivalent. Along the way we obtain several results about type $\mathrm{III}$ equivalence relations and graphings of independent interest. For example, we show that every ergodic type $\mathrm{III}_0$ graphing admits an ergodic hyperfinite subgraph for which the natural factor map of Krieger flows is an isomorphism.

title: Chain flaring fails on the rose for atoroidal irreducible automorphisms
summary: We show that the chain flare condition introduced by Clay fails for every topological representative on the topological $n$-rose of every power of an atoroidal irreducible automorphism of $F_n$.

title: Abelian quotients and orbit sizes for subgroups of linear groups
summary: Keller and Yang formulated two conjectures relating abelian quotients of subgroups of finite linear groups to largest orbit sizes. After counterexamples were found to the original conjectures, two revised versions were proposed. We prove both revised conjectures for every finite group $G$ satisfying $F(G)=F^*(G)$. We also extend a regular-orbit theorem for nilpotent subgroups to completely reducible modules of mixed characteristic under the same hypothesis.

title: The_Quadratic_Conjecture_and_p-groups_of_maximal_class
summary: The Quadratic Conjecture for finite p-groups, which is equivalent to the Strong Oliver Conjecture, asserts that if a finite p-group G acts faithfully on an F-module V, then the center Z(G) contains a quadratic element. In this paper, we investigate the structure of maximal class p-groups and establish that they satisfy the Quadratic Conjecture.

title: Non-discrete complex hyperbolic $(p_1,p_2,p_3;p_4)$-triangle groups
summary: In this paper, we study complex hyperbolic triangle groups of type $(p_1,p_2,p_3;p_4)$ with $3\le p_1\le p_2\le p_3\le p_4\le \infty$. We show that if the element $R_1R_2R_3$ is elliptic, then the group is either non-discrete or it belongs to a short list of known discrete groups.

title: Modular representations of metabelian groups
summary: Let $M$ be a module over a commutative ring with unity $R$, and let $φ:M \to R$ be an $R$-linear map. Then the product $mn = m + (1+φ(m))n$ defines a monoid $Mon(φ)$ on $M$. We show that if $G$ is a group, then $G$ arises as the group of invertible elements of some such monoid $Mon(φ)$ if and only if $G$ is metabelian.

title: Finite groups with exactly 2p + 1 subgroups of order p
summary: Let m_p(G) be the number of elements of order p in a finite group G, p prime. We prove that there is no finite simple group G with m_p(G) = 2p^2-p-1, and that a finite group with this property exists if and only if 2p+1 is prime or 3^f with f an odd prime. This concerns an open problem and extends the classification of finite groups with few elements of prime order.

title: Infranormal Kazhdan subgroups and instability in finite actions
summary: We prove that the group $G=\mathbb{Z}[1/2]^3\rtimes(\operatorname{SL}_3(\mathbb{Z})\times\mathbb{Z})$ is finitely presented and residually finite, but is not stable in finite actions, answering a question of Gohla and Thom. The proof uses the infranormal Kazhdan subgroup $H=\mathbb{Z}^3\rtimes\operatorname{SL}_3(\mathbb{Z})$ and its normal closure $N$ in $G$. A Kazhdan projection estimate shows that, in any $G$-action weakly contained in finite actions, every $H$-invariant measurable subset is also $N$-invariant. We construct an explicit sofic approximation of $G$ whose limit action contains a measurable subset that is $H$-invariant but not $N$-invariant.
